Financial Econometrics* 2(1)) Markov-Switching Multifractal volatility, never previously named in this ledger (`grep` for "multifractal"/"Calvet"/"MSM" returned zero hits) — replaces `kelly_regime_v4`'s single-span EWM `vol` estimator (feeding `conditional_target_scale`'s hysteresis state machine) with a `kbar=6`-component binomial multiplier cascade fit by grid-search Hamilton-filter MLE (no scipy in this environment, confirmed by R-118/R-125's own prior finding; `sigma_bar` profiled out in closed form to each window's sample std). **Attacks SIZE** (the vol-target input R-62 showed carries none of v4's headline signature but every hysteresis/deadband decision depends on), secondarily **COST** (a different vol estimate changes hysteresis-flip and deadband-crossing frequency). **Not a duplicate of** R-08/R-136 (additive, accuracy-chasing timescale/DVOL blends whose improvement itself was the problem — MSM is a multiplicative persistence cascade, and the novel branch here deliberately *discards* the transient component rather than blending it in more accurately), R-09 (range-based estimators, no range data used here), R-85 (critical slowing down on the VOTE's regime-timing, not the SCALE's own vol input), R-141/R-152/R-161/R-162/R-163/R-164/R-166/R-167/R-171 (every one of those caps or learns a multiplier on the *output* of the existing scale, or substitutes a statistic of the *strategy's own realized payoff*, rather than replacing what the underlying volatility estimate itself means). ### R-174 · 08-28 · NEGATIVE (both branches) — asymmetric sequential-evidence gate (Wald SPRT / GROW e-value) on `kelly_regime_v4`'s exposure INCREASES only fails a kill switch on both branches, and both fail for the SAME reason: the pre-registered evidence threshold cannot resolve within the deadband architecture's own episode lifetime

**Direction.** This session's scheduled brief was the generic "take the best strategy, propose an improvement direction, research it, dispatch conservative/novel sub-agents, measure, promote the winner." Step 0 found no in-flight round (HEAD == `origin/main`, unshallowed; newest `_shared.py` was `r173_shared.py`, with a section B entry, `grep -c "R-173"` = 10). Step 0b's saturation count was 1 consecutive null pass since R-173's own dispatch — "0-2: normal" — and the backlog grep returned only **B-48** (a documentation/formatting instrument fix, not a strategy-research item) plus the four already-inactionable rows (B-06 de-ranked, B-09 LOW, B-17 PARTIAL, B-28 blocked on data), so a fresh off-backlog literature-prompted round was warranted, the same convention R-160 through R-173 used. A background research sub-agent surveyed section B (R-88 through R-173) and section C for closed families; its top recommendation (a structural-break diagnostic on ETH's Sept-2022 PoS-transition date) is a measurement round with no natural conservative/novel implementation split, a poor fit for this session's brief, so this entry pursues its second candidate instead, sharpened using R-160's own explicit "next step" line: *"a future ERR-axis attempt on this architecture should look at gating the SCALE/sizing decision rather than the vote's direction, which no prior ERR-axis round (including this one) has touched."* **Attacks ERR** (primary: no error control exists anywhere in v4's `apply_deadband` re-sizing decision, which moves the position the instant `frac*scale` differs from it by more than 10%, symmetrically, in either direction), **SIZE** (secondary: it changes the sizing decision's timing). Deliberately asymmetric — gate only INCREASES, never decreases — motivated directly by R-33/R-57's own finding that this strategy family's edge is its ability to de-risk quickly ahead of a crash, so a symmetric gate (R-160's own shape) risks destroying the edge along with the noise it filters. **Not a duplicate of** R-28/R-31 (a single continuous e-process triggering a DECREASE action, retired for confounding with exposure), R-87 (Adaptive Conformal Inference on a continuous confidence set, no discrete gate), R-160 (online-FDR gating vote FLIPS symmetrically — this round gates the combined `frac*scale` decision, increases only), R-161/R-167 (RCPS/CRC capping SCALE's magnitude, evaluated fresh each bar with no path dependence — this round controls *when* an increase is allowed, never *how much*), R-171 (Online Newton Step learning the whole leverage path, no hypothesis-test framing), or R-172 (FCR bound on a discrete vote pattern's retrospective average, not a forward sequential accumulator). Full citations (Wald 1945 for the conservative branch's SPRT; Grünwald, de Heide & Koolen 2024 "Safe Testing", *JRSS-B* 86(5), for the novel branch's GROW e-value; MacLean, Thorp & Ziemba 2010 for why an increase specifically is the vulnerable direction) and the frozen pre-registration are in `experiments/r174_direction.md` and `experiments/r174_shared.py`, written and committed (`035274e`, "R-174 (WIP): announce in-progress round") before either branch was dispatched, per step 0's collision-avoidance convention.

**What was done.** Two disjoint files, each importing only from the read-only `r174_shared.py`: `experiments/r174_conservative_wald_sprt.py` (classical Wald 1945 SPRT: H0 `mu=0`, H1 `mu=MU1`, boundaries `A=ln((1-beta)/alpha)`/`B=ln(beta/(1-alpha))`, `beta=alpha`) and `experiments/r174_novel_safe_testing_gro.py` (a sequential Gaussian-mixture Bayes factor — H0 `mu=0`, H1 mixture `mu ~ N(0,TAU^2)` — thresholded at `1/alpha` per Ville's inequality, independently verified via WebSearch against Grünwald/de Heide/Koolen 2024 and Shafer, Shen, Vereshchagin & Vovk 2011, arXiv:0912.4269). Both wired through the shared, statistically-neutral `run_asymmetric_gate` state machine (`r174_shared.py`): decreases in `frac*scale` apply immediately exactly as v4's own `apply_deadband`; an increase beyond the 10% deadband opens a pending episode in which the branch's own accumulator runs bar-by-bar until it grants the increase, rejects it, or the request itself disappears. `MU1 = TAU = 8.0855e-06` (inner-train mean per-bar log-return, derived in code, not hand-copied) and `ALPHA_GRID = (0.10, 0.05, 0.20)` were frozen before either branch touched real data. Pre-registered decision rule (R-160's own shape, reused deliberately): PROMOTE-CANDIDATE requires, for at least one alpha on both markets, (a) a paired-bootstrap CI on `d_log_growth` excluding zero positive, (b) `d_sharpe >= +0.2` or a risk-matched drawdown improvement, and (c) the same-sign improvement reproducing on `eth_replication`. Falsification test = ETH sign-replication (clause c). Pre-registered kill switches: A1 (>=1 alpha must show >=3 delayed-and-resolved episodes on BTC inner-validation, else the gate never binds) and A2 (gated-path R² < 0.999 vs v4's own target, else degenerate). **Configs evaluated: 6** (3 alphas x 2 branches), each run fully through `compare()` on both markets and all three slices (inner-train, inner-validation, `eth_replication`) — **72 real-data cells total**. Neither branch read a bar at or after `OOS_START` (2023-01-01) at any point; both independently confirmed the max timestamp seen was 2022-12-31 23:55:00 UTC, enforced by `compare()`'s own `assert_no_holdout`.

**Result.** Both branches' mandatory `causal_truncation_probe_series` checks passed, and both branches' calibration self-tests on synthetic zero-drift noise behaved sanely (accept rates at or below nominal alpha, small-sample caveats disclosed in both files). **Kill switch A1 (gate binds) FAILED on both branches, decisively and for the same underlying reason.** Conservative: on BTC inner-validation, zero of 51-58 opened episodes ever resolved (neither accepted nor rejected) at any of the three alphas — Wald's boundaries (1.39-2.94 in log-likelihood-ratio units) are never reached before v4's own frequent decrease events cancel the pending episode. Novel: zero of 56 opened episodes in inner-validation ever resolved with any delay, at any alpha (2 of 157 resolved somewhere in the full pre-holdout window, both outside inner-validation). **Root cause, confirmed independently by both branches' own diagnostics, not an implementation bug:** `MU1`/`TAU` (~8.09e-6 per bar, BTC's own inner-train mean drift) is roughly three orders of magnitude smaller than the per-bar sigma (~1e-3) both tests use as their known-variance input, so resolving either test requires on the order of 10^4-10^5 consecutive bars of one-sided evidence — far longer than a "pending increase" episode survives before v4's own vote/scale architecture moves `desired` again. Kill switch A2 (non-degeneracy) PASSED on both branches, but in the opposite direction from a relabeling concern: R² against v4's own target was strongly *negative* (conservative: -1.05 to -0.53; novel: -0.90 to -0.67) — both candidates spend inner-validation almost entirely flat (`exposure_ratio` 0.00-0.11 in nearly every inner-validation/eth cell), not a rescale of v4 but a near-total collapse of exposure, because the gate that is supposed to delay an increase instead blocks it for the practical duration of the study. On real-data comparisons, **0 of 36 cells per branch** satisfy the decision rule's conjunction: every inner-train cell shows large, CI-excluding-zero-on-the-negative-side underperformance (d_sharpe -0.93 to -1.83, d_log_growth -2.1 to -3.1) purely from lost participation, inner-validation cells are mostly flat (`d_sharpe` -0.25 to +0.46, most CIs include zero, exposure near zero both arms), and every `eth_replication` cell is negative (d_sharpe -1.22 to -1.75), including the novel branch's ETH-futures cell, which is the one cell R-160 found a small *positive* signal on — a directly opposite pattern from R-160's own cross-branch asymmetry, not a replication of it. The conservative branch's alpha=0.20 cell is the closest any config comes to the bar (clause (b) clears on both markets, `d_sharpe` +0.46 spot / +0.28 futures) but clause (a) still fails (CI straddles zero) and clause (c) fails outright (ETH replication negative both markets) — a genuine fall-through, not rounded up to a nearer label. **Falsification test outcome: fails on every alpha that reaches it** — ETH sign-replication is uniformly negative, never a tie-breaker for a config that had already cleared (a)+(b) jointly (none did).

**Verdict.** **NEGATIVE, both branches, against their own frozen R-174 rules — no strategy registered.** One-line lesson, reusable beyond this specific pair of tests: **a sequential-evidence gate anchored to the market's own realized per-bar drift and volatility needs an episode lifetime the deadband/vote architecture cannot supply** — v4's regime episodes resolve on the scale of days to weeks (the deadband/vote's own hysteresis), while a per-bar drift-vs-volatility ratio this small requires an episode roughly two to three orders of magnitude longer to resolve either classically (SPRT) or via an anytime-valid e-value (GROW/safe testing); this is a property of the ratio between BTC's realized drift and its realized volatility at 5-minute granularity, not of which specific sequential test is used, and it generalizes the R-160 finding ("delaying a flip costs more than it buys") to "delaying *any* re-sizing decision on this signal, this asset, this bar size, costs more than it buys" — this project's tenth ERR-axis construction on this vote/scale architecture to close NEGATIVE (R-28/31, R-87 x2, R-104, R-105 x2, R-114 x2, R-160 x2, now R-174 x2: 0 of 11 promoted). A structurally distinct methodological finding, disclosed rather than smoothed over: the novel branch's own directional sanity check found its symmetric Gaussian mixture is a two-sided "has drift departed from zero" test, not a one-sided "is drift positive" test (`log_e` trends up under both `mu=+TAU` and `mu=-TAU` by comparable amounts) — protection against granting on negative drift comes structurally from `run_asymmetric_gate`'s own episode-cancellation, not from the accumulator's own math, worth naming for any future round that reuses a symmetric-mixture e-value for a one-sided decision. **Holdout counter: +0, running total unchanged at ~761** (R-173's own figure). Neither branch's decision rule was altered after seeing any number. Not registered — an ordinary-shape negative on an axis with a well-established base rate (0 of 11 ERR-axis attempts on this architecture, matching R-160's own precedent of not registering), not independently instructive enough for a table row per step 5's threshold. Code lives under `experiments/` per step 5. **Next step:** this specific generalization (asymmetric sequential gate on `frac*scale`'s timing, keyed to per-bar drift/volatility) is closed for BOTH a classical and a modern anytime-valid test; a future ERR-axis attempt on this architecture's SIZE/timing decision should anchor its evidence threshold to a statistic with a shorter natural resolution time than raw per-bar drift-vs-volatility (e.g. a coarser-horizon aggregate return, or a state-dependent alternative that shrinks as evidence accumulates) if it wants to test a genuinely different failure mode than "the threshold is unreachable within an episode's own lifetime." **B-48 remains the only OPEN backlog row** (a documentation/formatting instrument fix, not a strategy-research item); B-06/B-09/B-17/B-28 remain blocked, low-value or deliberately partial — unchanged by this round.

### R-173 · 08-28 · NEGATIVE (both branches) — causal Roll (1984) / Corwin-Schultz (2012) spread estimation as a COST-axis instrument changes nothing, on either branch

**Direction.** This session's scheduled brief was the generic "take the best strategy, propose an improvement direction, research it, dispatch conservative/novel sub-agents, measure, promote the winner." A research sub-agent tallied explicit axis-attack density across all 172 prior rounds and found **COST** the least-recently-worked axis with a genuine attempt count (4 direct rounds vs. SIZE's 30+, INFO's 15, N≈3's ~20+, ERR's 14; last dedicated COST round was R-145, 08-25) rather than an axis a fresh round had just declared exhausted. It proposed two purely price/range-based microstructure spread estimators neither cited nor implemented anywhere in this ledger: **Roll (1984)**, "A Simple Implicit Measure of the Effective Bid-Ask Spread in an Efficient Market," *Journal of Finance* 39(4), 1127–1139 (`spread = 2*sqrt(-Cov(dP_t, dP_{t-1}))`, from `close` alone), and **Corwin & Schultz (2012)**, "A Simple Way to Estimate Bid-Ask Spreads from Daily High and Low Prices," *Journal of Finance* 67(2), 719–760 (a closed-form estimator from consecutive-bar `high`/`low` ranges). The idea attacks **COST** ("costs scale *with* the signal") by replacing this project's flat fee-tier cost model with a causally-estimated, time-varying friction measure. Not a duplicate of L-14/L-15/L-16 (`camouflage_flow`/`stealth_trend`/`flow_regime`: order-flow *direction* proxies, an INFO-axis signal, not a spread estimator), R-56/R-77 (patient-limit execution: fill *probability*, not a cost estimate), R-64/65/67/68/165 (Gârleanu-Pedersen: an *assumed* quadratic-cost functional form, never a measured cost), R-131/133/134/151 (turnover throttle: a fixed resource budget, no cost estimator), or R-145 (funding cost by venue). The 08-26 verification pass (section E archive) had named Roll/Amihud/Kyle/VPIN/Almgren-Chriss together and dismissed all five as needing order-book data in one sentence — wrong for two of the five, since Roll needs only `close` and Corwin-Schultz needs only `high`/`low`; that pass evaluated zero configurations and is not a round. `grep -n "Roll (1984)\|Corwin.*Schultz" docs/LEDGER.md` returned zero hits before this round. Two variants were designed: **conservative** (re-price `kelly_regime_v4`'s own already-realized rebalance history at the measured illiquidity — a pure cost audit, no strategy-logic change) and **novel** (a spread-conditioned dynamic deadband — widen the existing 10% re-target threshold when estimated friction sits high in its own trailing percentile, deferring exactly the trades a real elevated spread would make more expensive). Full non-duplication argument, the frozen Step-0 degeneracy/falsification measurement on real BTC data, and both branches' pre-registered decision rules are in `experiments/r173_direction.md`, written and frozen by the operator (based on the sub-agent's proposal, independently checked against the ledger) *before* either branch was dispatched.

**What was done.** Operator-authored, frozen shared module `experiments/r173_shared.py`: `roll_spread_causal` and `corwin_schultz_spread_causal` (both `.shift(1)`-lagged, matching `r102_shared.v4_symmetric_vol`'s own causality convention; Corwin-Schultz's raw 2-bar estimator, designed for daily bars, is smoothed with a 1-day rolling mean before use at 5-minute resolution — disclosed in the module docstring), `spread_percentile_causal` (a bar's own trailing percentile rank of the spread series), `apply_deadband_dynamic` (v4's `apply_deadband` generalized to a spread-percentile-scaled threshold; `k=0.0` reproduces the original **exactly**, checked in `_self_test` and independently re-verified below), and the frozen Step-0 measurement helpers. **Step-0 measurement, real BTC data, before either branch was dispatched:** Roll's rolling-covariance window is negative (spread defined) on **76.3%** of bars; Corwin-Schultz's raw 2-bar estimate is positive (informative) on **63.2%** of bars pre-smoothing, **99.99%** post-smoothing — neither estimator is degenerate at 5-minute resolution. Stress-episode elevation ratios (smoothed Corwin-Schultz, ±3-day window vs. whole-period daily median) on the project's own canonical six-episode calendar: 2018 bear onset 3.35x, 2018 bear bottom 0.91x, COVID crash 3.10x, 2021-11 top 0.72x, Terra/Luna 1.48x, FTX collapse 1.13x — **median 1.31x**, clearing the frozen `>1.0` falsification gate (4 of 6 episodes individually elevated; the 2018 bottom and the 2021-11 top are the two non-elevated cells, disclosed rather than dropped). Both branches dispatched. Conservative: `experiments/r173_conservative_illiquidity_refee.py` — sampled Corwin-Schultz (primary) and Roll (secondary cross-check) at every one of v4's own real deadband-triggered rebalance bars on the training period, `|Δtarget|`-notional-weighted into an illiquidity add-on rate, then re-ran the **unmodified** registered `kelly_regime_v4` under an illiquidity-adjusted `MarketSpec` (built via this project's own existing `fee_at()` primitive, the same one `fee_study.py`'s 0.40% sensitivity tier uses) against `buy_and_hold`, at three tiers (baseline, illiquidity-adjusted, 0.40% sensitivity), train-only first, then one frozen holdout read. Hit and fixed one real blocker: `r102_shared.run_slice`'s unconditional `assert_no_holdout` guard rejects any input frame reaching `OOS_START` at all, making it categorically unusable for the branch's own one permitted holdout read — fixed with a local, field-for-field reproduction (`run_slice_holdout`) inside the branch's own file, used only by its holdout command, guarded by its own belt-and-suspenders assertion that any `start >= OOS_START` call is explicitly marked as a holdout read; neither `r173_shared.py` nor `r102_shared.py` was touched. Novel: `experiments/r173_novel_spread_deadband.py` — `build_target(df, k) = apply_deadband_dynamic(v4_raw_desired(df), spread_percentile_causal(corwin_schultz_spread_causal(df)), k=k)`, swept `k∈{0.5,1.0,2.0,4.0}` against `v4_target` via `r173_shared`'s inherited `compare()` harness (inner-train/inner-val/ETH replication, both markets, paired bootstrap), `k*` selected on BTC inner-validation only (mean ΔSharpe: 0.5→−0.0175, 1.0→−0.0202, 2.0→+0.0911, 4.0→+0.0977), plateau-checked against its neighbour (k=2.0 retains 93% of the k=4.0 peak, same sign). **Both branches' operator-level independent re-verification** (not a separate skeptic sub-agent, given both closed NEGATIVE with no promotable claim to adversarially re-check, but real code execution against the actual committed files, not merely reading the reports): `build_target(df, k=0.0)` reproduces `v4_target(df)` **bit-for-bit** on real BTC data (`np.array_equal == True`, independently re-run); `instrument_addon()` re-run directly on real BTC data reproduces the conservative branch's reported numbers **exactly** (n_events=809, cs_addon=0.00038597, roll_addon=0.00044777, corr_full=0.6758, corr_at_events=0.4545, both to full float precision). **Configurations evaluated: 86** (conservative: 48 — 36 train-only backtests across 3 tiers × 2 markets × 2 slices [BTC inner_train+inner_val, ETH replication] × candidate+control, plus 12 holdout backtests; novel: 38 — 5 k-values × 6 `compare()` cells [3 slices × 2 markets] = 30, plus 4 train-period `buy_and_hold` comparison legs × 2 = 8). `pytest tests/test_causality_strict.py`: **55 passed**, run by both branches independently, before and after the conservative branch's `run_slice`-bypass fix.

**Result.** **Conservative.** Illiquidity add-on (Corwin-Schultz, primary): BTC **3.86bps** half-spread (809 rebalance events, train-only), ETH **3.41bps** (483 events, full pre-holdout replication); Roll (secondary): BTC 4.48bps, ETH 5.61bps — moderate positive agreement between the two independent estimators (correlation 0.68/0.37 full-series BTC/ETH, 0.46/0.49 at the sampled event bars), disclosed, not blocking. Spot and futures carry the identical fractional add-on by construction (`v4_target` never reads `MarketSpec`, and `kelly_regime`'s own `order_notional` routing is leverage-normalized — verified directly, not assumed). CS-smoothing-window sensitivity (0.5x/1x/2x): 4.03/3.86/3.68bps, stable within ~9%. Fee tiers actually used (read from `tradebot/broker.py`, not assumed): baseline spot 0.10%/futures 0.05%; illiquidity-adjusted BTC spot 0.1386%/futures 0.0886%. **Train-only** (inner-train + inner-val + ETH, 18 cells): spot stays **COIN-FLIP** at all three tiers, every slice; futures_5x **BEATS** at all three tiers on inner-train/ETH and stays **COIN-FLIP** at all three tiers on inner-val (the OOS-analog slice) — no sign flip anywhere. **The one frozen holdout read** (BTC, 2023-01-01 onward, 12 cells): spot Δlog −0.129→−0.171→−0.451 across the three tiers (baseline→adjusted→0.40%), all **COIN-FLIP**; futures_5x Δlog −1.127→−1.182→−1.127 (0.40% tier leaves futures' own 0.05% fee unchanged, per every prior fee-tier round's own convention), all **COIN-FLIP** — no flip at any tier, on either market. Per the frozen Step-4 CONSERVATIVE rule, this reads directly as **NEGATIVE / no new caveat**: the flat-fee approximation this project already uses was adequate at the illiquidity level actually measured. **Novel.** `k=0.0` reproduces the control exactly (independently re-verified above). At `k*=4.0` (the training-selected, plateau-checked value), Stage A's frozen 4-clause promotion gate: (a) beats `buy_and_hold` train-period, CI excludes zero on all 4 cells → **FAIL** (3 of 4 cells' CIs include zero; only ETH futures clears); (b) ΔSharpe ≥+0.2 or a risk-matched ≥5pp drawdown reduction on all 4 cells → **FAIL** (drawdown is *worse* by 4–11pp on every one of the 4 cells, none risk-matched); (c) survives ETH replication → PASS (+0.18 spot, +0.23 futures); (d) plateau not peak → PASS. **2 of 4 clauses clear, reported as the genuine fall-through it is** (ROUTINE.md's own R-151-derived rule), not rounded to a label. Per R-33's own standing risk-matching rule, the apparent gains at k=2.0/4.0 are an artifact, not an edge: vol_ratio against the v4 control runs 1.11–1.39 (well outside the project's own [0.9,1.1] matched-risk band) concentrated almost entirely on ETH, with trade count collapsing 75→52→37 as `k` rises — exactly this ledger's own named base-rate failure for COST-axis throttles (R-56, R-77, R-131, R-133): the mechanism suppresses precisely the trades that carry the edge, and larger `k` only manufactures the appearance of one by taking on more realized volatility and a worse drawdown. Per the frozen two-stage rule, since no `k` cleared the training-period bar, **the holdout was never read** for the novel branch.

**Verdict.** **NEGATIVE, both branches, against their own frozen R-173 rules — no strategy registered, no new README/LEDGER cost caveat filed.** **One-line lesson:** two textbook, decades-old, purely price/range-based spread estimators are real (non-degenerate at 5-minute resolution, elevate during genuine stress episodes on this project's own calendar) but immaterial at the scale `kelly_regime_v4` actually trades — its ~3.5–4.5bps measured illiquidity add-on is small enough, relative to the 809-event train-period rebalance frequency, that re-pricing at it moves no comparison's sign at any tier on either market; and trying to trade *around* that same friction by deferring rebalances reproduces this ledger's now-fifth instance of the unmatched-risk COST-throttle artifact rather than escaping it. Funding (R-13/R-14) remains the one cost this project has found that materially changes a verdict; spread/illiquidity, measured directly for the first time here rather than assumed away, does not — a genuinely different answer from the same axis, not a restatement of the funding finding. **Holdout counter: +12, running total ~761** (conservative: 12 reads — BTC spot and futures_5x, candidate+control, at all three fee tiers; novel: +0, no `k` cleared the training-period bar, holdout never touched; ~749 was the running total after R-172). Neither branch's decision rule was altered after seeing any number. **Next step:** not filed as a new backlog item — this was an off-backlog literature-prompted round (Step 0b's consecutive-null-pass count was 1 at dispatch, "0–2: normal"). **B-48 remains the only OPEN backlog row** (a documentation/formatting instrument fix, not a strategy-research item); B-06/B-09/B-17/B-28 remain blocked, low-value or deliberately partial — unchanged by this round.


### R-172 · 08-28 · NEGATIVE (both branches) — FCR-adjusted selective inference on `kelly_regime_v4`'s vote pattern fails both branches

**Direction.** This session's scheduled brief was the generic "take the best strategy, propose an improvement direction, research it, dispatch conservative/novel sub-agents, measure, promote the winner." A research sub-agent read the standing diagnosis, section C's ruled-out table, and the last ~30 rounds of section B, corrected the brief's own stale premise that the ERR axis had "only 2 attempts" (it found and the operator independently confirmed **13 prior ERR-axis rounds**: R-31, R-87, R-104, R-105, R-106, the 7-round R-109–R-123 novelty-discount family, R-114, R-116, R-147, R-160, R-161, R-167 — zero promotions, zero partial passes), and proposed a genuinely untested statistical basis: **False Coverage-statement Rate (FCR) control** (Benjamini & Yekutieli 2005, *JASA* 100(469), 71–81) and **Post-Selection Inference / PoSI** (Berk, Brown, Buja, Zhang & Zhao 2013, *Annals of Statistics* 41(2), 802–837) applied to a previously-undiagnosed structural feature of `kelly_regime_v4` itself: its 3-anchor vote (`frac`) is the mean of three independently-latched binary votes, so at any bar the strategy runs on one of **8 discrete anchor-agreement patterns**, and no round has asked whether trusting the currently-realized pattern's own historical forward-return edge is honest once the fact that it is *one of 8 implicitly-compared candidates* is accounted for — a textbook post-selection/winner's-curse problem, attacking **ERR** (no error control anywhere in the signal path). Both citations were independently verified by the operator (web search against each paper's own abstract/formula, not merely trusted from the sub-agent's report) before freezing anything. Full non-duplication argument against all 13 prior ERR-axis rounds, plus R-171 (closed this same session, different constraint/slot, and this design deliberately avoids both of R-171's own named traps), is in `experiments/r172_direction.md`, written and frozen by the operator (`grep -in "benjamini\|yekutieli\|post-selection\|selective inference\|berk.*brown.*buja\|false coverage" docs/LEDGER.md` returned zero hits before this entry). Two variants were designed: **conservative** (a literal binary FCR-corrected gate on the vote — trust `frac` fully if the active pattern's FCR-adjusted one-sided lower confidence bound excludes zero on the positive side, force flat otherwise) and **novel** (the FCR interval's own two-sided *width* modulates `kelly_regime.py`'s already-shipped, currently-dormant `vote_gamma` convex-response exponent per-bar instead of as a fixed scalar — a different insertion point and a different statistic, sign vs. magnitude, from the conservative branch). Simulable purely from OHLCV: both anchor votes and the forward-return labels used to build each pattern's causal historical bucket come from the same close series every prior round has used.

**What was done.** Operator-authored, frozen shared module `experiments/r172_shared.py` (`anchor_pattern` — the 8-way classification, reproducing v4's own `_latched_anchor_vote` bit-for-bit rather than reimplementing it; `fcr_lower_bounds` — the causal, embargoed, FCR-corrected per-pattern one- and two-sided confidence bound, at daily resolution matching `r161_shared.py`'s own `daily_close`/`daily_last_of` convention; `norm_ppf` — a self-contained Acklam inverse-normal-CDF, since this project ships no scipy, self-tested against four independent known reference quantiles before anything downstream trusts it; kill-switch helpers `binding_fraction`/`relabeling_r2`). `Q_FCR=0.10` (matching `r161_shared.py`'s own `HB_DELTA=0.10` precedent, not fitted), `M_PATTERNS=8` (the full candidate space, fixed per Berk et al.'s "valid under any selection rule" argument, not the observed-so-far count), `HORIZON_DAYS=5`, `MIN_N=30` — all disclosed and fixed before either branch ran; a real-data check at freeze time confirmed the primitive is non-degenerate (83% of inner-train days clear `MIN_N`, and among those ~48% show the gate trusting the vote). Two independent implementation branches, each in an isolated git worktree, each on its own file (`experiments/r172_conservative_fcr_gate.py`, `experiments/r172_novel_fcr_gamma.py`), neither editing the shared module, the design doc, or each other's file. **Pre-registered decision rule (frozen in `r172_direction.md` before either branch ran):** PROMOTE only if (1) ΔSharpe vs `kelly_regime_v4` on inner-validation ≥ **+0.2** on **both** BTC and ETH, **or** a matched-exposure max-drawdown reduction ≥5pp on both markets; (2) survives the branch's falsification test; (3) plateau, not peak, across a frozen 3-point bracket; (4) sign does not reverse at the 0.40% taker fee tier. **Falsification tests, pre-registered:** conservative — sign(ΔSharpe BTC inner-val) must equal sign(ΔSharpe ETH replication); novel — sign of ΔSharpe must not reverse between the standard and 0.40% fee tiers.

**A shared causality defect, found by one branch, independently confirmed missing and fixed in the other before trusting its numbers.** The conservative branch's own implementer, running `causal_truncation_probe_series` end-to-end on **real** BTC data (not just the smooth synthetic self-test data), caught a one-day lookahead: `fcr_lower_bounds`'s daily `(lcb, ucb, n_used)` for day D is computed from day D's *own* last bar, so naively broadcasting it onto day D's *own* bars uses information from the end of day D to gate exposure at the start of day D — invisible on smooth synthetic paths (latched anchor votes almost never flip mid-day) but real on choppy BTC data. The fix (lag the daily index by one calendar day before broadcasting, the same `.shift(1)`-family convention this codebase uses everywhere) was applied in that branch's own file. The operator then checked the novel branch's file directly and found the identical unshifted broadcast, uncaught because that branch's own causal probe had only been run on smooth synthetic frames — applied the identical one-line fix, and **re-verified** the fix on real BTC data: `causal_truncation_probe_series` now passes on the real series (it did not before, once tested); the PRIMARY `compare()` table and the fee-tier falsification check were both re-run post-fix. The fix changed the novel branch's magnitudes materially (BTC inner-val futures ΔSharpe: −0.51 → −0.17; its bootstrap CI stopped excluding zero) but did **not** change the decisive clause-1 verdict, confirmed by the operator's own re-run — see Result. The novel branch's 3-point `k`-bracket (clause 3) was **not** re-run post-fix and is disclosed as such; this is immaterial to the round's verdict since clause 1 already fails cleanly on both the pre- and post-fix inner-validation numbers.

**Configurations evaluated: 59 backtest cells total.** Conservative: 4 distinct configurations (PRIMARY `q=0.10`, a `q∈{0.05,0.20}` robustness bracket, one 0.40%-fee-tier re-run), 19 cells, plus its own sanctioned holdout read (4 cells) = 23. Novel: 3 distinct configurations pre-fix (`k∈{0.5,1.0,2.0}`) plus a fee-tier re-run, 22 cells, superseded on PRIMARY and the fee-tier check by a 10-cell post-fix operator re-verification (6 `compare()` cells + 4 fee-tier cells), plus its own sanctioned holdout read (4 cells, post-fix) = 36. Both branches independently ran `causal_truncation_probe_series` end-to-end through their own strategy wiring (not just the shared primitive alone) and both kill switches (KS-A binding fraction ≥2%, KS-B relabeling R²<0.95) before any comparison. `uv run pytest`: **540 passed**, including `test_causality_strict.py`.

**Result.** Neither kill switch tripped on either branch. **Conservative**, KS-A (binding fraction) = **0.176**, KS-B (relabeling R²) = **0.708** — genuinely binds, genuinely not a relabeling. PRIMARY (`q=0.10`) inner-validation: ΔSharpe = **−0.34** (BTC spot), **−0.47** (BTC futures), **−0.33** (ETH spot), **−0.20** (ETH futures) — negative on every cell. Falsification test *passes* (both markets negative, same sign — not the single-asset-overfit failure this test screens for, though the branch simply loses on both assets). The plateau check *fails* outright: across `q∈{0.05,0.10,0.20}`, BTC inner-val ΔSharpe runs **+0.40/+0.41 → −0.34/−0.47 → +0.07/−0.03** — PRIMARY sits at the single worst point of its own 3-point bracket, a peak on the wrong side, not a plateau. 0.40% fee tier: no sign reversal (already negative at the standard tier). Holdout, read once per the frozen rule (falsification test passed, so the branch was not killed pre-holdout): ΔSharpe **−0.09** (spot), **−0.11** (futures), drawdown modestly *better* (−4.36pp/−4.44pp) but not risk-matched (exposure ratio 0.76) and both bootstrap CIs contain zero. **Novel** (post-fix numbers authoritative), KS-A = **0.834**, KS-B (R²) = **0.910** (both computed pre-fix; not expected to move materially post-fix since the fix only shifts which bars a given day's value applies to, not the value itself). PRIMARY (`k=1.0`, post-fix) inner-validation: ΔSharpe = **−0.03** (BTC spot), **−0.17** (BTC futures), **−0.16** (ETH spot), **−0.13** (ETH futures) — negative on every cell, though far milder than the pre-fix numbers (BTC futures pre-fix: −0.51, its 95% CI excluding zero on the losing side; post-fix: −0.17, CI containing zero). Falsification test *passes*, post-fix: no sign reversal between standard and 0.40% fee tiers on either market (spot −0.029→−0.056; futures −0.166→−0.173). The plateau check, on the **pre-fix** bracket only (disclosed limitation): BTC inner-val and ETH both get monotonically *more negative* as `k` increases (inner-val mean ΔSharpe −0.250 → −0.379 → −0.543; ETH −0.045 → −0.193 → −0.209) — a genuine, consistent trend, but in the wrong direction for promotion, while inner-train's own mean crosses zero across the bracket (+0.000 → +0.010 → −0.116), failing the strict same-sign plateau test on that slice. Holdout, read once per the frozen rule (post-fix code): ΔSharpe **+0.07** (spot), **+0.06** (futures), drawdown better (−2.28pp/−1.11pp), and — unlike the conservative branch — genuinely risk-matched (exposure ratio 0.93, vol ratio 0.97 both markets), but both bootstrap CIs contain zero and the point estimate sits nowhere near the pre-registered +0.2 bar. Both branches' decision rules were evaluated exactly as frozen; neither was altered after seeing any number, and the one post-hoc change made (the broadcast-lag fix) tightened the causal correctness of the primitive rather than the threshold, per ROUTINE.md's fix-before-trusting-a-result allowance, and was independently verified not to flip the decisive clause.

**Verdict.** **NEGATIVE, both branches, against the frozen R-172 rule — no strategy registered.** Both fall through cleanly (clauses 2 and 4 met on both branches; clause 1 fails decisively on both — no cell on either branch clears +0.2 or a risk-matched ≥5pp drawdown reduction with a CI excluding zero; clause 3 fails on the conservative branch outright and is unresolved-but-trending-the-wrong-way on the novel branch) — genuine fall-throughs, not rounded up to the nearest label per ROUTINE.md's own rule. **One-line lesson:** this ledger's now-14-round-deep ERR axis has tested a materially different statistical basis — simultaneous-validity correction over a *finite combinatorial candidate space* (8 discrete vote patterns), as opposed to every prior attempt's aggregate significance, leave-one-out disagreement, market-state novelty, regime duration, parametric shrinkage, sequential online-FDR, or output-side tail-loss cap — and gotten the same answer: the vote's own signal, once split 8 ways and error-corrected, is not precise enough on this project's realized history to say anything the unmodified vote didn't already say, at any of the two insertion points tried (a hard pre-scale gate, or a per-bar convex-response exponent). A second, reusable lesson survives independent of the mechanism: **a same-day daily-resolution statistic broadcast onto its own day's bars is a one-day lookahead unless explicitly lagged**, and it is specifically invisible to a causal-truncation probe run only on smooth synthetic data, because the bug requires a mid-day pattern flip to manifest — future daily→bar broadcast constructions in this codebase should run their causality probe against real, choppy price data at least once, not only the synthetic generator every `_self_test` uses by convention. **Holdout counter: +8, running total ~749** (conservative: 4 reads — BTC spot and futures_5x, candidate+control, at PRIMARY; novel: 4 reads — BTC spot and futures_5x, candidate+control, at PRIMARY, post-fix; ~741 was the running total after R-171). **Next step:** not filed as a new backlog item — this was an off-backlog literature-prompted round (Step 0b's consecutive-null-pass count was 1 at dispatch, "0–2: normal"). **B-48 remains the only OPEN backlog row** (a documentation/formatting instrument fix, not a strategy-research item); B-06/B-09/B-17/B-28 remain blocked, low-value or deliberately partial — unchanged by this round.


### R-171 · 08-28 · NEGATIVE (both branches) — Online Newton Step leverage selection on `kelly_regime_v4`'s SCALE factor converges to persistently elevated exposure and worse drawdown on both markets; novel branch's own pre-registered stress-window falsification test trips 24/24

**Direction.** This session's scheduled brief was the generic "take the best strategy, propose an improvement direction, research it, dispatch conservative/novel sub-agents, measure, promote the winner" (same brief R-167/R-170's entries name). A research sub-agent read the standing diagnosis, section C's ruled-out table and the recent rounds (R-160 through R-170), searched the literature, and proposed replacing `kelly_regime_v4`'s conditional-volatility-target `scale` (`min(target_vol/vol, max_leverage)` under v3's hysteresis vol-state machine) with a scalar `b_t` learned online, causally, by the **Online Newton Step (ONS)** algorithm for portfolio management (Agarwal, A., Hazan, E., Kale, S. & Schapire, R. E. (2006), "Algorithms for Portfolio Management Based on the Newton Method," ICML 2006, 9–16), applied to the single-asset (leverage-vs-cash) case of the vote's own already-decided realized bet-payoff. Attacks **N≈3** primarily (a pathwise, distribution-free regret guarantee that needs no repeated independent regime draws to be *valid* — the one property no plug-in moment estimator this ledger has tried can claim) and **SIZE** secondarily. Full non-duplication argument (against L-11/R-149's grid-integration mixture, R-28/R-31's retracted sequential-testing sizer, R-152/R-153's CDaR pair, R-93's closed Grossman-Zhou family, R-164's closed vol-scaling-substitution family ["inverse leverage effect"], R-166's vol-response sign flip, the CPPI/Hurst-CPPI pair, Busseti-Ryu-Boyd, CRRA/Merton, "per-vote-state Kelly fraction," the closed walk-forward-refit and minimax-reselection items, and R-147's James-Stein vote-side shrinkage) is in `experiments/r171_direction.md` (moved there from the repo-root scratch location at Step 5, per R-170's own convention, not deleted; `experiments/r171_shared.py`'s own docstring still cites the original `docs_scratch_direction.md` path, frozen and unedited, matching `r170_shared.py`'s identical stale-path precedent); `grep -c "Newton\|Agarwal\|Online Newton Step\|ONS\b" docs/LEDGER.md` returned zero hits outside that document as of R-170. Two variants were designed: **conservative** (one shared ONS accumulator across the whole series, replacing `scale` outright) and **novel** (three independent ONS accumulators, one per v3's own existing hysteresis vol-state, "sleeping experts" per Freund, Schapire, Singer & Warmuth 1997 — updating only on bars where that state is active). Simulable purely from OHLCV: the update needs only the vote's own bar-by-bar `frac_t` (already computed causally in `prepare()`) and the asset's own realized next-bar return, both already in the existing frame.

**What was done.** Operator-authored frozen shared module `experiments/r171_shared.py` (the `ons_scale` primitive; `asset_simple_return`, deliberately a SIMPLE not log return, disclosed explicitly as the unit this codebase's ledger has been burned by silently mismatching before; kill-switch helpers `corner_lockin_fraction`/`exposure_artifact_r2`; the pre-registered constants). `eps`/`beta`/`b0` were derived, not swept: the AHKS 2006 paper's own Theorem 1 (located and read in full) parameterizes an n≥2-stock simplex with a market-variability floor that does not map onto a single scalar with signed returns, so — per the design doc's own explicit fallback instruction — the module uses the general exp-concave Online Newton Step form from Hazan, E., *Introduction to Online Convex Optimization* (2nd ed. 2023, arXiv:1909.05207), Ch. 4, Algorithm 12/Thm. 4.5: exp-concavity constant `alpha=1` (an exact elementary-calculus fact for `-log(1+b*r)`, not assumed), gradient bound `G=0.09843...` (measured on BTC bars strictly before `INNER_VAL_START`, i.e. inner-train only), domain diameter `D=max_leverage=2.0`, giving `beta=0.5`, `eps=1.0`, `b0=max_leverage/2=1.0`. Two independent implementation branches, each on its own file (`experiments/r171_conservative_ons.py`, `experiments/r171_novel_ons_sleeping.py`), neither editing the shared module or each other's file. **Pre-registered decision rule (frozen in `r171_shared.py`'s named constants before either branch ran):** PROMOTE only if (1) ΔSharpe vs `kelly_regime_v4` ≥ **+0.2** (R-20's own noise floor) on inner-validation on **both** BTC and ETH, **or** a matched-exposure (`exposure_ratio`/`vol_ratio` both in `[0.9,1.1]`, R-33's convention) max-drawdown reduction ≥5pp on both markets; (2) survives its branch's falsification test; (3) plateau, not peak (conservative: 3-point `eps` bracket; novel: 3-state vs. collapsed 2-state agreement); (4) sign does not reverse at the 0.40% taker fee tier. **Falsification tests, pre-registered:** conservative — sign(ΔSharpe BTC inner-val) must equal sign(ΔSharpe ETH); novel — max drawdown must not be deeper than unmodified v4 in more than 12 of 24 Monte Carlo stress windows, on either market. **Configurations evaluated: 208 total across both branches** (conservative: 4 — PRIMARY plus a 3-point `eps`-robustness bracket [0.5×/1×/2×], plus one additional 0.40%-fee-tier holdout re-run; novel: 204 — 2 vol-state-conditioning configs [3-state PRIMARY, collapsed 2-state] × 6 `compare()` cells each = 12, plus 192 Monte Carlo stress-window comparisons [2 configs × 4 asset/market cells × 24 windows] for its pre-registered falsification test). Both branches independently re-verified causality via `causal_truncation_probe_series` run end-to-end through their own strategy wiring (not just the shared `ons_scale` primitive alone), and each ran its own kill switches (KS-a corner lock-in >80%, KS-c exposure-artifact R²>0.95 against v4's own incumbent scale path) before proceeding to any comparison.

**Result.** Neither kill switch tripped on either branch: corner lock-in was negligible everywhere (0.00–0.34% of bars, conservative and novel, all vol-states), and `exposure_artifact_r2` was strongly *negative* (−4.92 to −5.35) — the learned `b_t` path is structurally unlike v4's own incumbent scale, not a relabeling of it. **Conservative branch**, PRIMARY config: inner-validation ΔSharpe = +0.264 (BTC spot), +0.139 (BTC futures_5x), +0.097 (ETH spot), +0.294 (ETH futures_5x) — falsification test *passes* (all four cells agree in sign) — but `exposure_ratio` ran 2.2–3.5× and `vol_ratio` 1.6–3.4×, **never** inside the [0.9,1.1] matched-exposure band on any cell, so the DD-reduction promotion alternative is categorically unreachable, and drawdown was in fact worse everywhere (+12 to +50pp). The plateau check *fails*: BTC futures_5x ΔSharpe flips sign across the `eps` bracket (0.5×: −0.043; 1×/PRIMARY: +0.139; 2×: −0.076) — the PRIMARY's one positive futures cell sits between two negatives, a peak, not a plateau. Holdout was read once (PRIMARY config, per the frozen rule): spot ΔSharpe = −0.022 (ΔDD +3.09pp, worse), futures_5x ΔSharpe = −0.196 (ΔDD +7.96pp, worse), both bootstrap CIs contain zero, exposure still unmatched (1.08–1.48×); the 0.40% fee-tier check shows no sign reversal (−0.196 vs −0.187) only because the candidate already loses at both tiers. **Novel branch**: the pre-registered falsification test trips decisively — **24 of 24** stress windows show deeper max drawdown than unmodified v4, on **all four** asset/market cells (BTC spot, BTC futures_5x, ETH spot, ETH futures_5x), far past the >12-of-24 kill threshold — so per the frozen rule the branch is killed before the one permitted holdout look; **zero** holdout bars were read. Inner-train/inner-validation/ETH numbers (reported for completeness, not decisive): exposure_ratio ran 2.09–3.15× v4's own everywhere (never risk-matched, RM=false on all 12 rows); ΔSharpe strongly negative on inner-train (−0.41 spot, −0.61 futures), mixed/marginal on inner-validation and ETH (+0.07 to +0.28), drawdown worse by +12.8 to +48.1pp on every cell, no CI excluding zero anywhere. The plateau clause itself *holds* (3-state and 2-state agree in sign and magnitude on every slice) but is moot given the falsification failure. Both branches' decision rules were evaluated exactly as frozen; neither was altered after seeing any number.

**Verdict.** **NEGATIVE, both branches, against the frozen R-171 rule — no strategy registered.** Conservative falls through cleanly (clauses 2 and 4 met, clauses 1 and 3 not met — a genuine fall-through, not rounded up to the nearest label per ROUTINE.md's own rule); novel fails outright at its own pre-registered falsification gate. **One-line lesson:** ONS's headline property — validity without needing repeated independent regime draws, because its guarantee is pathwise against the single realized sequence — is also exactly why it offers no defense against that one sequence being unrepresentative: on this project's realized BTC/ETH history the algorithm converges to persistently elevated leverage (mean `b_t`≈1.5–1.7, 2–3× v4's own exposure, in every configuration tested, both branches) because a fixed-in-hindsight leverage near the domain's upper boundary genuinely was the best response on *this* realized path — the identical Kelly-overbetting fragility (MacLean, Thorp & Ziemba 2010) every plug-in moment estimator in this ledger has already failed on, arrived at by a structurally different mechanism (a regret bound instead of a moment estimate) that was specifically chosen to avoid it. **This closes the online-convex-optimization / no-regret family of SIZE-axis primitives** as a class distinct from the ~28 already-closed plug-in-estimator attempts — a future session should not retry ONS, mirror descent, or a similar regret-minimizing portfolio-selection algorithm on this strategy's scale slot expecting a different loss or projection to rescue it without first arguing why that construction would not also converge toward the realized path's own best-in-hindsight (boundary-adjacent) leverage; the two escapes that would actually change this — an explicit tail-risk/drawdown penalty in the loss, or a domain cap tighter than v4's own `max_leverage=2.0` — either reintroduce the estimation-risk problem ONS was chosen to avoid, or simply reproduce a hard-coded leverage cap, a mechanism every prior CPPI/CDaR closure already tried. **Holdout counter: +6, running total ~741** (conservative branch: 6 reads — BTC spot and futures_5x candidate+control at PRIMARY, plus the futures_5x 0.40%-fee-tier candidate+control re-run; novel branch: +0, killed at its own falsification gate before any holdout read; ~735 was the running total after R-165, unchanged through R-166–R-170). `uv run pytest` re-run as an extra check even though neither branch touched a registered strategy or `src/` framework file (matching R-170's own convention of not strictly requiring it): **539 passed**, including `test_causality_strict.py`; `tests/test_ledger_format.py` passes against this entry. **Next step:** not filed as a new backlog item — this was an off-backlog literature-prompted round (Step 0b's consecutive-null-pass count was 2 at dispatch, "0–2: normal"). **B-48 remains the only OPEN backlog row** (a documentation/formatting instrument fix, not a strategy-research item); B-06/B-09/B-17/B-28 remain blocked, low-value or deliberately partial — unchanged by this round.


### R-170 · 08-28 · NEGATIVE (Step-0 gate, before Step B, both branches) — multiplicative meta-labeling confidence layer on `kelly_regime_v4`'s `frac*scale`, from funding/VRP/illiquidity/episode-excursion features: none carries out-of-fold discriminative skill above a label-permutation null, at 11/11 tested configurations

**Direction.** This session's scheduled brief was the generic "take the best strategy, propose an improvement direction, research it, dispatch conservative/novel sub-agents, measure, promote the winner" (same brief R-167's entry names). A research sub-agent read the standing diagnosis, section C's ruled-out table and R-154 through R-169, searched the literature, and proposed meta-labeling (Lopez de Prado 2018, *Advances in Financial Machine Learning*, ch. 3) as a multiplicative confidence layer applied strictly post-`frac*scale` (`desired' = frac*scale*m`, `m in [0,1]`, ahead of v4's own unmodified 10% deadband), never blended into the vote — the architectural fix R-80's own closing line named and left undone. Attacks **SIZE and ERR** jointly: SIZE because the multiplier only ever shrinks an already-decided bet, never generates one; ERR because it is a formally out-of-fold-validated probability rather than an ungated heuristic, on the *magnitude* decision rather than the *timing*/*tail-cap* decision every one of the eight prior ERR-axis constructions used. Full write-up, including the "why not a duplicate" case against R-04, R-80, the 4-for-4-failed bounded-brake family (R-34/R-41/R-53-cons/R-73-cons), R-87/R-160/R-161/R-167, R-162/R-141/R-163, B-09 and R-100/R-145, is in `experiments/r170_direction.md` (kept as the design record, not deleted). Two variants were designed: **conservative** (one 4-feature logistic classifier, purged/embargoed refit every 90/180/365 days, literal `m = clip(2(p-0.5),0,1)`) and **novel** (four single-feature "sizing experts" — funding, VRP, illiquidity, episode-excursion — blended online via Hedge/multiplicative-weights, `hedge_experts`' own precedent, each expert only ever shrinking, never reversing, so it cannot repeat L-09/R-130's "no-regret guarantee is relative to the best expert, and every expert loses to fees" failure). Not simulable purely from OHLCV — funding, DVOL and volume are all already-committed files, so no new capability was needed.

**What was done.** Operator-authored frozen shared module `experiments/r170_shared.py` (causal feature builders for funding-rate z-score, DVOL-minus-realized-vol VRP, Amihud illiquidity, and R-163's own episode-relative-excursion state variable reused as a classifier feature; a triple-barrier meta-label at each non-flat vote-flip event, vertical barrier = min(H_DAYS, next flip); a hand-rolled purged/embargoed logistic regression + label-permutation-null Step-A gate, reusing R-80's own validated design verbatim; the mandatory Step-0 gates named in the design doc). Two disclosed pre-dispatch corrections, made before any branch was dispatched and before any performance number existed (ROUTINE.md's own allowance): (1) purge/embargo is applied directly in bar-time rather than via `tradebot.inference.purged_train_mask`, because vote-flip events are irregularly spaced and that helper assumes one row per regular time unit; (2) the Step-A gate and every refit train on bars < `INNER_VAL_END` (inner-train + inner-validation combined) rather than inner-train alone, because DVOL's history only starts 2021-03-24 — inside inner-validation — so an inner-train-only gate would see 0% VRP coverage and never test it at all; ROUTINE.md Step 3 itself names inner-validation a training resource. Before dispatching either implementation branch, the operator ran the module's own mandatory Step-0(i) and Step-0(iii) gates as a non-degeneracy check (R-168's own precedent for this step): identity check (`m≡1` reproduces `kelly_regime_v4` exactly, diff = 0.0, confirmed), then the Step-A AUC-vs-permutation-null gate, PRIMARY config first, then robustness diagnostics (varying feature set, `H_DAYS`, L2, `n_groups`) run after and not changing the frozen decision, exactly as R-80's own convention specifies. **Configurations evaluated: 11** — all Step-A gate measurements (1 primary 4-feature-where-finite classifier; 4 single-feature experts, one per novel-branch channel; 2 `H_DAYS` alternates 5/20; 2 L2 alternates 0.3/10.0; 2 `n_groups` alternates 6/10) — no strategy backtest, no `ev()` call, and no holdout bar was read at any point; the pipeline's own correctness was independently confirmed on a synthetic case with a known, deliberately injected 1-feature logistic signal (recovered AUC 0.807 against a null p95 of 0.540, `pass=True`) and a synthetic pure-noise feature (AUC 0.483, `pass=False`, matching the null's own downward-biased center under this exact fold structure) before trusting any real-data number. All four causal feature builders and the flip/label construction independently passed the project's standard truncation causality probe.

**Result.** The PRIMARY Step-A gate (BTC, bars < `INNER_VAL_END`, `n_groups=8`, `L2=1.0`, `H_DAYS=10`, all 4 features where finite, `n=153` admissible flip-event samples, base rate 51.0%) measured out-of-fold **AUC = 0.4699** against a 500-draw permutation null's 95th percentile of **0.5880** (empirical p = 0.568) — the gate does not merely fail to clear, the true statistic sits *below* the null's own mean (0.484). Every one of the novel branch's four single-feature experts, run through the identical gate independently (funding_z: AUC 0.432, n=264, p=0.747; VRP: AUC 0.421, n=153, p=0.810; illiquidity: AUC 0.424, n=557, p=0.947; episode-excursion: AUC 0.462, n=557, p=0.503), failed at least as decisively — illiquidity and excursion had the largest sample sizes (100% coverage, no funding/DVOL gap) and still failed by the widest margins. Every robustness diagnostic on the combined classifier (H_DAYS 5/20, L2 0.3/10.0, n_groups 6/10) also failed, with point AUC estimates ranging 0.404–0.474, none within reach of its own null's p95. 11 of 11 tested configurations landed below the null's 95th percentile; 10 of 11 landed below the null's own mean. ETH coverage is disclosed separately, not run as a gate: the project's standard ETH replication file (`ethusd_bitfinex_5m.csv.gz`) ends 2019-12-31, entirely before both funding (2020+) and DVOL (2021-03+) exist, so a meta-labeling classifier on ETH would necessarily train on illiquidity and excursion alone — moot here since BTC itself never cleared Step-0(iii) at any tested configuration.

**Verdict.** **NEGATIVE, both branches, at the mandatory pre-registered Step-0(iii) gate — no strategy code was built.** Per this round's own frozen stop rule (reusing R-80's novel branch's identical rule and R-166's precedent for stopping at Step 0), a branch that fails the AUC-vs-permutation-null gate STOPS before Step B; since the gate fails for the combined classifier *and* independently for each of the four single-feature experts the novel branch's own Hedge blend would combine, dispatching either implementation branch would only reproduce this same measurement inside a strategy wrapper — the project's own convention (R-75/R-79/R-80's novel branch) is explicitly not to do that. **One-line lesson:** this is B-09's own standing diagnosis (quoted directly in R-80's entry — "the binding problem is not that trust is miscalibrated but that correctly-calibrated trust is low") confirmed a second time, on a materially different label construction (event-triggered triple-barrier at vote flips, not R-80's daily-sampled label) and a materially different feature set (funding/VRP/illiquidity/excursion, none price-anchor-derived, chosen specifically to avoid R-162's collinearity failure) — the failure is not R-80's combination-formula bug (already fixed here, per the identity check) and not feature collinearity with v4's own vote/scale (these features are structurally independent of the anchors); it is that whether a v4 vote-flip pays off, net of fees, over the next 5-20 days, is not predictable from any of these four channels on this data, individually or combined, at the purged/embargoed sample sizes (153-573) this project's own trade frequency provides. **Holdout counter: +0, running total unchanged at ~735** (R-165's own figure; R-166 through R-169 also read none, per that list's standing convention of noting a skipped range in the next round that does increment it — this round continues that range rather than adding its own bullet). Neither the frozen Step-0 gate nor the never-reached Step-4 decision rule moved after any number was seen. `pytest -q` was not re-run (no registered strategy or shared framework code was touched — `experiments/r170_shared.py` is not auto-discovered). **Next step:** this closes the meta-labeling axis for a THIRD time (R-04's lookahead bug, R-80's combination-formula bug, this round's clean feature-information test with both prior bugs fixed) — a future session should not retry multiplicative or confirming-vote meta-labeling on this architecture expecting a different feature set to rescue it without first arguing why that feature set's information content differs structurally from funding/VRP/illiquidity/episode-excursion, the broadest non-price-anchor-derived set this project's committed data supports. Not filed as a new backlog item. **B-48 remains the only OPEN backlog row** (a documentation/formatting instrument fix, not a strategy-research item); B-06/B-09/B-17/B-28 remain blocked, low-value or deliberately partial.


### R-169 · 08-28 · INSTRUMENT FIX — four defects in the routine's own machinery: a step-0 check wrong by 69 rounds for eight days, section E's row format ratcheting back into the prose it replaced, and R-41's `|basis|` column shift still hiding two rounds' conclusions in sections C and D

**Direction.** Not a strategy round. Step 0b's 3+ tier bars a new literature
sweep and names three things a pass may still do; *"fix the instrument"* is
one of them, and the section says an exhausted backlog is the best time for
it. This is the seventh consecutive null pass since R-168, so the sweep was
barred and the instrument was audited instead. Attacks no market constraint —
it attacks the **procedure**, the same axis as R-151 (a backlog grep because
prose kept lying about the table), R-158 (a table because prose kept burying
the backlog) and B-44 (a measurement of the harness rather than the market).
Not a duplicate of any of them: R-151 fixed how the backlog is *read*, R-158 fixed
where null passes are *written*, and both fixed the format by writing a
better instruction. Every defect below is one of those instructions failing
after it was written, which is why this round's output is a test rather than
a paragraph.

**What was done.** Audited the machinery Step 0 and Step 5 actually execute —
`docs/ROUTINE.md`'s command blocks, and every table in the ledger — by
running the commands and parsing the tables rather than reading them. Four
defects, all measured:

- **D1 — Step 0's first check was wrong by 69 rounds, for eight days.** The
  routine's highest-priority check ("an undispatched frozen pre-registration
  outranks both the backlog and any new idea") ran as
  `ls experiments/*_shared.py | tail -3`. `ls` sorts lexicographically, so
  with `r168_shared.py` on disk it printed **`r97, r98, r99`** and had not
  shown a file above `r99_shared.py` since 08-20. It fails in the
  safe-looking direction: it names a file that *does* have a section B entry,
  so the check returns "nothing in flight" and looks like it worked. The one
  state it exists to catch — a freshly frozen `r1nn_shared.py` nobody
  dispatched — is precisely the state it cannot see. Spotted by pass 6 in its
  own section E row; not fixed there, because a null-pass row cannot change a
  command.
- **D2 — section E's rows inflated 28x, monotonically.** Section E's opening
  paragraph says the signal "is one row wide". Measured over its 33 numbered
  rows, newest-first: the six oldest average **119 characters**, the six
  newest **3,359**, with no reversal in between (84 → 246 → 998 → 2,300 →
  4,370). Six null passes since R-168 deposited 22.2 KB. This is R-158's own
  failure mode — 1,285 lines of interchangeable prose that looks like
  diligence — reconstituted inside the table built to prevent it, and it
  violates this file's standing rule that prose belongs in a section and
  never in a table cell.
- **D3 — the seven newest rows had six cells against a five-column header.**
  Every one of them carried a trailing `full detail: none (zero
  configurations evaluated; …)` cell that the header does not declare.
  Markdown drops the surplus on render, so that text has never been visible
  to any reader — the same silent column-shift class (`|basis|`, R-41/R-44)
  that ended section B's life as a table. Nobody caught it in seven passes
  because nobody could see it.
- **D4 — and the original `|basis|` shift is still live, in sections C and
  D, hiding measured conclusions.** Found by extending D3's parse to the
  other registry tables rather than assuming section E was special. Three
  rows write maths in prose with absolute-value bars — `\|Δf\|` (C, R-128),
  `\|exposure*lambda*next_day_return\|` (C, R-161), `\|Δleg\|` and
  `\|ΣΔleg\|` (D, B-46) — and an unescaped `|` is a cell separator, so those
  rows carry 5, 5 and **9** cells against 3- and 5-column headers. This is
  not cosmetic. B-46's note renders as far as *"gate the combined re-target
  once, either on gross leg turnover (`Σ"* and then stops: R-154's actual
  result — gross-turnover weakly dominating net-exposure on all six cells —
  is in the file and has never been on the page, in the backlog table Step 0
  sends every session to read. The two C rows truncate R-128's and R-161's
  *why-it-was-ruled-out* text in the ruled-out registry, which is the table a
  research sub-agent reads in full precisely to avoid re-opening a closed
  direction. R-41/R-44 named this failure in 08-20 and fixed section B by
  abandoning tables; the rows that stayed in tables kept the bug for eight
  days.

The common mechanism is the finding: **each pass writes its row by copying
the row above it**, so a defect introduced once is inherited by every
subsequent pass and grows monotonically. Neither D2 nor D3 is reachable by
asking future sessions to be briefer or more careful — D2 *is* six sessions
being careful, and D3 is seven sessions being invisible to themselves. D4 is
the same point over a longer baseline: a rule the file states about itself,
in the file, and then violates in the file. So the fix is mechanical:
`tests/test_ledger_format.py`, four CI-enforced checks —
(1) every row in sections A, C, D and E has exactly its header's cell count
(fence-aware, so E-verbose's quoted originals are read as evidence rather
than as rows); (2) every section E cell is ≤ **300 characters** (~5x looser than the 84–246 the format ran at when
R-158 built it, so it would never have bound a working pass); (3) the live
block's pass numbers descend and its top row's number equals the block's
height, which is the invariant Step 0b's counter silently assumes; (4) every
numeric-sorted `r<nn>_shared.py` has a matching `### R-nn` section or an
`IN PROGRESS: R-nn` stub — D1's check, run in CI, and it accepts the stub
because that is the announce-in-branch rule R-131/R-133 introduced. The 22
non-conforming rows were normalised to a lede plus a pointer, with every
original row reproduced **verbatim** in the new `E-verbose` subsection
(script-generated and byte-compared, not retyped); nothing is deleted.
`docs/ROUTINE.md` Step 0 gained the numeric sort and a warning; Step 5 and
section E's header gained the cap and the reason for it. **Configurations
evaluated: 0** (no strategy, no market data, no holdout read).

**Result.** Both format tests fail on the pre-fix ledger (`section E row '6',
column 'step 0' is 581 characters against a 300 cap`; the width test flags
all seven six-cell rows, and after those are fixed it still flags C's two and
D's one, which is how D4 was found) and pass on the fixed one — verified by
stashing the fixes, running them, and restoring. The prereg guard was
verified the same way against a planted `r999_shared.py` and failed as
designed. The live section E table's mean row went **1,269 → 462 characters,
max 4,372 → 877**, and `E-verbose` holds all 22 originals with a byte-exact
match against the pre-fix file. D4's three rows were fixed by escaping eight
bars (`\|`) and change no content — 5 → 3, 5 → 3 and 9 → 5 cells — which
restores R-128's and R-161's ruled-out rationale and R-154's measured
conclusion to the rendered page for the first time. Step 0b's `awk` counter
returns **6** before the round's own `—` row is added and **0** after, which
is the correct reset, so the normalisation did not disturb the one consumer
of this table. Full suite green. No falsification test applies: this round
makes no claim about markets, and its claims about the files are checked by
the tests themselves. Sections C and D were **measured but not capped** —
their longest cells run 3,234 and 606 characters — because capping them means
relocating registry text, which is a round of its own; filed as **B-48**.

**Verdict.** **INSTRUMENT FIX.** The lesson is narrower than "write better
instructions" and it is the third time this project has learned it: *a format
rule that is only prose decays at the rate the format is copied.* R-151
needed a grep, R-158 needed a table, and both of those fixes then decayed in
turn — R-158's table is what D2 and D3 happened to. The version that holds is
the one CI can fail. **Holdout counter: unchanged at its prior total (0
consultations added; no market data was read).** Decision rule did not move —
there was none to move. Next step: **B-48**, the one part of this deliberately
left undone — sections C and D carry the same prose-in-a-cell problem an
order of magnitude larger (3,234 and 606 characters), and capping them is a
content migration rather than an escape. If a future pass finds itself
editing `E-verbose` or raising `CELL_CAP`, that is the signal it is writing a
round, not a null pass.

### R-168 · 08-28 · NEGATIVE (both branches) — cross-venue price fusion on `kelly_regime_v4`'s VOTE: a striking, statistically significant BTC-only effect that fails the frozen cross-market replication gate on ETH in both branches, independently

**Direction.** Replace the single-venue Coinbase-spot close feeding `kelly_regime_v4`'s VOTE (the 20/40/80-day anchor construction) with a causal fusion of that same spot close and Deribit's independently-transacted `BTC-PERPETUAL`/`ETH-PERPETUAL` close (`data/btcusdt_deribit_perp_5m.csv.gz`, `data/ethusdt_deribit_perp_5m.csv.gz`), leaving SCALE (the conditional-volatility-target multiplier, still computed from the original spot return series), the 1% band, the vol-regime hysteresis and the 10% deadband/latch all byte-for-byte unchanged. Attacks **INFO** in the standing diagnosis's most literal sense ("one price series") for the first time as a change to the vote's own construction, rather than as a brake/confirming-vote bolted on top of it. Not a duplicate of R-41/R-42 (Deribit-basis *spread magnitude* as a SCALE brake — a different quantity, computed as `log(perp/spot)`, from fusing the two venues' price *levels* into the vote's own anchor input), R-146 (anchor *statistic* over the one existing series), R-147 (anchor *combination weights* over the one existing series), or R-145 (venue *routing* of the unmodified target across spot/futures legs, COST axis — never touches how the vote is computed). Citations: Alexander & Heck (2020, *J. Financial Stability* 50) and Frino, Gaudiosi, Webb & Zhou (2025, *J. Futures Markets* 45(4)) on time-varying, volatility-conditioned venue price-leadership, motivating the novel branch's weighting scheme.

**What was done.** Operator-authored shared module `experiments/r168_shared.py` (frozen pre-registration, causal fusion loaders for BTC and ETH, the vote-construction replica, a causal-truncation probe, and a `signal_check` paired-bootstrap comparator against unmodified `kelly_regime_v4`), imported read-only by both branches, neither of which edited it or each other's file. A Step-0 non-degeneracy check (run by the operator before either branch was dispatched, reported in the shared module's own docstring) found the fused vote correlates 0.9894 with the unmodified one on the 83.2%-overlap BTC window — high, but not degenerate: 3.22% of bars carry a full anchor-vote flip and the discrete flip count drops 240→204, concentrated exactly at the boundary-crossing bars this project's twelve failed regime-timing mechanisms were trying to time better — so the round proceeded to both branches rather than killing at Step 0. **Conservative** (`experiments/r168_conservative_venue_fusion.py`): equal-weight fusion, `fused = (spot_close + perp_close_aligned) / 2`, degrading to spot alone wherever perp is unavailable (pre-2018-08-14 BTC / pre-2019-03-14 ETH); zero new tunable parameters. **Novel** (`experiments/r168_novel_venue_fusion.py`): a volatility-regime-conditioned fusion weight reusing `kelly_regime_v3`'s own existing hysteresis vol-state machine (`w_perp = w_low` in the low-vol state, `0.5` in the normal band, `w_high` in the high-vol state), swept over a pre-registered 5-point symmetric grid `(w_low,w_high) ∈ {(.5,.5),(.3,.7),(.2,.8),(.1,.9),(0,1)}`; the `(.5,.5)` cell doubles as a cross-branch identity check (confirmed bit-identical to the conservative branch's own construction, max abs diff = 0.0). Both branches ran the standard two-opposite-tampers causal-truncation probe (PASS in both) and a build-time bug was caught and fixed in the conservative branch (a first draft recomputed rolling anchors over the `df`-sliced window rather than the fused series' own full reloaded timeline — the exact mistake step-0's dispatch brief warned about — fixed and reverified via a warmup-prefix-vs-full-history parity check on the vote fraction specifically). **Configurations evaluated: 7** (conservative: 1 primary + 1 perp-only bracketing check; novel: 5-point grid). Inner-train/inner-validation only (2017–2020 / 2021–2022); **the 2023-01-01+ holdout was not touched by either branch or by the operator.** The operator independently reproduced the decisive BTC futures_5x and ETH futures_5x cells from a clean shell for the conservative branch's primary config — every number (d_sharpe, drawdowns, paired-bootstrap CI, time-in-market) matched the branch's own report exactly, including the causal-probe result.

**Result.** Both branches land on essentially the same numbers for the equal-weight fusion (the novel branch's `(.5,.5)` grid point *is* the conservative branch's mechanism, confirmed identical). BTC, inner-validation, futures_5x: `d_sharpe = +0.839` (Sharpe 1.09 vs v4's 0.25), max drawdown 17.2% vs v4's 32.3%, paired-bootstrap 95% CI on Δlog-growth `[+0.317, +0.715]` (excludes zero), exposure matched (time-in-market Δ −0.54pp). BTC spot: `d_sharpe = +1.148`, drawdown 17.0% vs 33.2%, CI `[+0.505, +0.861]`. Both are large, clean, statistically significant improvements — the kind of result this project has learned to distrust exactly because of how good it looks in isolation. ETH, the same primary config, same inner-validation window (fully inside ETH-perp's 2019-03-14+ coverage, so this is *not* the disclosed coverage-start artifact): `d_sharpe = +0.051` (futures_5x) / `+0.027` (spot), drawdown improvement 1.4–2.6pp (an order of magnitude smaller than BTC's 15–16pp), paired-bootstrap CI `[-0.004, +0.110]` / `[-0.007, +0.060]` — both contain zero. The novel branch's grid is a clean, monotone plateau on BTC futures_5x (`d_sharpe` +0.839 → +0.734 as `w_high` rises from 0.5 to 1.0) running in the *opposite* direction from its own hypothesis: leaning the fusion weight toward the perp venue during high volatility (per Alexander & Heck 2020) monotonically **weakens** the result, and the best-performing point on the grid is the one that isn't the novel mechanism at all — flat 50/50. Bracketing check (BTC futures_5x): spot-only (v4, weight=0) Sharpe 0.251 → equal-weight fusion (weight=0.5) 1.091 → perp-only (weight=1.0) 2.318, a clean monotone ladder, a useful implementation sanity check but also evidence the effect scales smoothly with "how much perp" rather than triggering at some threshold, arguing against a specific volatility-conditioned mechanism and for something closer to a generic, asset-specific rescaling of the vote's own dynamic range.

**Verdict.** **NEGATIVE, both branches**, against the frozen inner-validation gate's condition 1 (matching-direction, matching-magnitude improvement on BTC **and** ETH): BTC clears it by a wide margin on both branches; ETH does not, on either. This is precisely the failure mode R-33/R-57 built this project's cross-instrument replication discipline to catch — a single-asset effect that would have looked, on BTC alone, like the best SIZE/INFO result in this file's history (a drawdown *halving* with a tight, significant CI). **One-line lesson:** venue-fusion changes BTC's regime timing in a way that is real, large, and reproduced bit-for-bit by two independent implementations, but it is not a general "second venue improves the vote" effect — it is asset-specific, and conditioning the fusion weight on volatility (the novel branch's whole contribution) makes it *worse*, not better, ruling out the mechanism this round's own citations predicted. Whether the BTC-only effect is itself real (a genuine BTC-specific information advantage from Deribit's perpetual) or an artifact of BTC's longer/cleaner perp history is not resolved by this round and would need the six-instrument Coinbase panel (per R-57's own precedent) to settle — not proposed here as a next step given the panel's already-measured 1.47-of-8 Grinold breadth (R-63) makes a further single-mechanism panel round low-value on its own merits. **Holdout counter: +0, no change to the running program-level total (~735, per R-165/R-167's own count)** — neither branch read it, and the operator's independent reproduction above was confined to the same inner-validation window both branches already used. Decision rule did not move after any result was seen. **Next step:** this closes the vote-input-SOURCE sub-family of the INFO axis (as distinct from the vote's statistic, R-146, or its combination weights, R-147, both already closed) for the venue-fusion construction specifically; a future session should not re-try flat or vol-conditioned cross-venue fusion on this vote architecture expecting a different weighting scheme to rescue ETH — the novel branch's monotone, wrong-direction grid argues the failure is not a tuning problem. Backlog (section D) unchanged — this was an off-backlog, literature-prompted round (Step 0b's consecutive-null-pass count was 1 at dispatch, "0-2: normal"), and B-06/B-09/B-17/B-28 remain the only live rows, all blocked, low-value or deliberately partial.

**What was done.** Pre-registration frozen and committed

confidence budget at a FIXED calendar cadence spends it faster than the
sample grows and never unlocks any exposure over the whole 4-year
inner-train window at PRIMARY (alpha=0.05) — worse than R-161's own
diagnosed floor. Fixed before freezing by spacing refits GEOMETRICALLY
(doubling) instead — Howard et al.'s own named construction, not an ad hoc
patch — and re-verified to partially unlock at the looser ALPHA_GRID cell
before the pre-registration was written down. Two branches, each 6 configs
(`TAU_GRID={0.05,0.08} × ALPHA_GRID={0.05,0.10}` primary grid, 2
robustness cells), 36 real-data cells each (3 slices × 2 markets):
`experiments/r167_conservative_howard_cap.py` (peeled-Hoeffding,
expanding window, geometric-doubling refit schedule) and
`experiments/r167_novel_betting_cap.py` (fixed-fraction betting confidence
sequence, expanding window, fixed 30-day refit cadence — Ville's
inequality needs no peeling, so no doubling schedule is required for this
engine). **12 configs, 72 real-data cells total across both branches.**
Decision rule: PROMOTE-CANDIDATE requires, on inner-validation, for at
least one config on both markets, (a) strictly lower tail-loss exceedance
than v4-uncapped AND (b) dSharpe ≥ +0.2 / a bootstrap-excludes-zero

than peeled-Hoeffding's on the same data at matched tau/alpha/delta — WSR's

suite green (536 passed) before dispatch.

identical defect rather than a new one; raw lambda mean/std served as the
non-degeneracy evidence instead, same workaround R-161 used.) **NOVEL
