one repository is the process finding its own limit — see the step-0 change
this round makes to `ROUTINE.md`. **The honest framing is therefore a replication,
not a round**, and it is recorded as one: R-131 stands as the round of record
for the direction, the literature (Khubiev, Semenov, Podlipnova & Khubieva
2025, arXiv:2509.04541; Boyd, Busseti, Diamond, Kahn, Koh, Nystrup & Speth
2017, *Found. Trends Optim.* 3(1)), the non-duplication argument and the
COST-family closure. This entry records what a second, independent execution
adds. Nothing here was written after reading R-131's entry except this
paragraph and the comparison table below.

**What was done.** Six files under `experiments/`, disjoint from R-131's:
`r133_stepA_turnover_census.py` (the A2 census, run before any performance

`r133_novel_turnover_throttle.py`, `r133_skeptic_audit.py`. Reports in

Same splits, same cells, same frozen decision rule (A2 ∧ B1 ∧ B3 ∧ B4 ∧ B5,
B2 diagnostic only) and same frozen falsification test (B4, ETH sign
replication). **56 candidate backtests over 17 distinct configurations**
(conservative 12/5, novel 14/7, skeptic audit 30/5 new). Max timestamp read,
every code path, both markets: `2022-12-31 23:55:00+00:00`.

*The implementations differ substantially*, which is what makes the agreement
worth something. R-131's branches inherit v4's `prepare()` untouched and
intercept its `on_bar` trigger, reading live broker exposure
(`ctx.position*ctx.close/ctx.equity`) and carrying an `owed` flag; this round
splices the throttle into a copy of v4's own latch loop inside `prepare()` and
acts on the latched target. R-131 gates on trailing turnover at bars `< i`
strictly; this round reads the EWM before folding bar `i`'s own event in —
the same one-step lag, reached differently. R-131's B3 sweeps corridor width
at 0.5x/1x/2x/4x; this round sweeps 2.0x–4.0x of v4's natural rate in five
steps plus a separate `eta` grid. So the two are not the same program run
twice.

**constant-`λ` ablation control** with the turnover-feedback channel deleted,
per R-130's methodological finding. It can only tighten the bar.

**Result.** **NEGATIVE, both branches — the same verdict R-131 reached, by
every gate.** The decision rule did not move.

*Where the two executions agree, on numbers neither could see from the other:*

| cell | R-131 | R-133 |
|---|---|---|
| conservative, BTC spot inner-val `d_sharpe` | −0.0284 | −0.028 |
| conservative, stress-episode deferrals (±3d, 6 episodes) | 0 | 0 |
| conservative, B4 | FAIL, ETH sign inverts (+0.0628) | FAIL, ETH sign inverts (+0.037) |
| novel, `λ` behaviour at stress episodes | saturates at `LAMBDA_MAX`=20 at 2 of 6 | saturates at 20 at 2 of 6 |
| novel, B1 / B3 / B4 | FAIL / FAIL / FAIL | FAIL / FAIL / FAIL |
| holdout consulted | +0 | +0 |

The conservative branch's decisive cell agreeing to three decimals across two
independently written implementations is the strongest reproduction evidence
this project has produced; the two `λ`-saturating episodes are not the same
pair (R-131: 2018 bear onset + FTX; R-133: 2018 bear onset + the 2021-11 top,
with FTX partially throttled at `λ`-mean 2.52), which is the expected
consequence of the two implementations throttling different objects, and the
phenomenon — *the throttle engaging hardest exactly where L-01/R-62 place v4's
edge* — is identical.

*What this execution adds, four findings R-131 did not measure:*

1. **Neither throttle reduces turnover, and this is the mechanical reason the
   family fails — a stronger claim than "the corridor barely binds."** Counted
   in fills: the conservative branch's ~5000 interventions at its tightest
   corridor buy a fill ratio of **0.832**, because deferral *postpones* an
   order rather than cancelling it; the move executes a few bars later. The
   novel branch is worse than a no-op — its fill ratio is non-monotone and
   never far below 1 (0.863–1.125), and **at the tightest corridor it is
   1.125, i.e. the throttle trades MORE than the strategy it throttles.**
   Shrinking an order does not remove it, it *splits* it. Partial adjustment
   also never reaches zero, so the position is never fully closed (30
   round-trip episodes against v4's 52, 1 for the constant-`λ` controls) and
   time in market rises 55.6% → 75.8%. R-131 concluded the family fails
   because v4 trades too rarely for a corridor to bind usefully; that is true
   and this adds that *even where it binds, it does not deliver the cost
   saving it exists for*.
2. **A unit error, caught mid-round and recorded.** The first version of the
   above divided by `Metrics.num_trades`, which counts round-trip **episodes**,
   not orders. That made the ablation controls read as "1 trade — the strategy
   freezes", which is false: they fill 240–352 times and merely never exit.
   Turnover is `len(result.fills)`; the two differ by ~300x on exactly the
   mechanisms a COST round studies. Both units now sit side by side in every
   table. Same class of error as R-128's unit-inconsistent transplant, and it
   survived a full write-up before the metric's definition was checked.
3. **R-33's risk-matching rule applies to ablation controls, not only
   benchmarks — and there it fails silently toward a false negative.** All
   five constant-`λ` controls score a *higher* `d_sharpe` than the live
   branch, which reads as "the feedback channel is decoration" until exposure
   is checked: every control sits **99.5–100% in market against v4's 55.6%**
   and carries +2.5 to +4.6pp more drawdown. An ablation is meant to weaken a
   claim, so an unmatched one does not announce itself the way an unmatched
   benchmark does.
4. **`broker.REBALANCE_DEADBAND` quantified, and filed as B-43.** The floor
   absorbs **4.5%** of v4's own intended re-targets but **61%** of the novel
   branch's at its frozen corridor and **83%** at its tightest — a confound
   *proportional to the mechanism's own parameter*, so it does not cancel in a
   comparison. R-130's skeptic measured the same defect on `hedge_experts`
   (96.8%); this is the second object. It is not what makes this family
   negative — finding 1 is — but it does mean no size-acting COST mechanism on
   this framework can be cleanly attributed. R-130's entry refers to it as
   "R-66/B-29"; that attribution is loose (B-29 was a snap-to-flat destination
   question, closed by R-66) and the deadband has never had a backlog item
   until now.

*Also audited, and worth recording because it is the number a careless
write-up would have headlined:* the conservative branch's best grid point
(corridor 2.0x, `d_sharpe` +0.137 on BTC spot inner-val, this round's largest
positive figure) is, run frozen on every other cell, positive on 4 of 6
inner-validation cells, **significant on 0 of 6**, negative on both ETH cells
and negative on inner-train (−0.022). The BTC-pass/ETH-invert shape again.

*Reproduction.* `pytest` 516 passed; `tests/test_causality_strict.py` 51
passed. Both mechanisms pass an explicit 90k-bar truncation probe (targets
bit-identical), and the online EWM recursion is verified equal to
`pandas.ewm(span, adjust=True)` — the full-series-fit hunt run against the one
statistic either branch computes.

**Verdict.** **NEGATIVE, both branches, confirming R-131.** One-line lesson,
and it is about the mechanism rather than this object: **a throttle on an
order the strategy has already decided to make cannot attack COST — deferring
postpones and shrinking splits — so the attack has to be on the decision, not
on the order that follows it.** The second lesson is procedural: two sessions
independently executed the same frozen pre-registration on the same day
without either seeing the other, and the fact that this is *detectable at all*
— same file, same rule, comparable numbers — is the pre-registration doing its
job. The waste is real and the fix is cheap (see the ROUTINE.md change this
round makes); the replication it accidentally produced is worth more than the
duplicated compute cost.

### R-131 · 08-25 · NEGATIVE (both branches) — constraining `kelly_regime_v4`'s realized trading rate to an admissible turnover CORRIDOR (a rate/resource cost model, not another per-trade EV threshold): a hard defer once trailing turnover exceeds the corridor (conservative) and an online dual-variable throttle that shrinks fills in proportion to a shadow price on turnover (novel); both fail cleanly, and the novel branch's own named risk — the throttle suppressing exactly the trades that carry the edge — is directly confirmed at two of six stress episodes

**Direction.** `kelly_regime_ev` (promoted) gates each rebalance by its OWN
marginal expected value against a fee/vol/horizon threshold
(`|df| > 2*fee/(H*sigma^2)`, Constantinides 1986; Davis & Norman 1990). This
round asks a different question: constrain the strategy's *rolling realized
turnover rate* to an admissible corridor and intervene only once recent
trading has been running unusually heavy — a resource constraint on
multi-bar history, not a per-decision threshold. Cites Khubiev, Semenov,
Podlipnova & Khubieva (2025/2026, arXiv:2509.04541, "Finance-Grounded
Optimization For Algorithmic Trading") for band turnover regularization
(a penalty zero inside an admissible corridor, biting only once exceeded)
and Boyd, Busseti, Diamond, Kahn, Koh, Nystrup & Speth (2017, *Foundations
and Trends in Optimization* 3(1), "Multi-Period Trading via Convex
Optimization") for turnover-penalized trading as a resource-constrained
control problem — the novel branch is the causal, online, dual-variable
analogue of that framing rather than a closed-form solve. **Attacks COST**
(costs that scale with the signal) via a cost-model family this project has
never tried. **Not a duplicate of:** `kelly_regime_ev`/L-05/L-06 (per-trade
marginal EV, inert to multi-bar trailing history by construction);
Gârleanu-Pedersen partial adjustment (R-65/R-67/R-68, a closed-form LQ
solution at a stationary derived rate, vs. an online history-reactive
corridor/dual-variable here); Almgren-Chriss adaptive execution urgency
(R-56/R-77, B-24 — changes HOW one already-decided trade fills, not
WHETHER/HOW MUCH to rebalance conditioned on trailing history); width-profile
banding (R-66 — band width is a function of the current target level `f`,
not of trailing realized turnover, a different state variable entirely);
`hedge_experts` pre/post-blend banding (R-128/R-129) and R-130's own
weight-update-level/combinator-wrapping constructions (same session as this
round, landed first — see process note below) — all four of those
transplant cost mechanisms onto `hedge_experts`, a different object; this
round keeps the object (`kelly_regime_v4`) and introduces the turnover-rate
cost-model family R-129's own closing line named as the open door. Full
non-duplicate reasoning, both mechanisms, and the named failure modes are
frozen verbatim in `experiments/r131_shared.py`'s own module docstring,
written and committed before either branch was implemented.

**Process note, disclosed in full.** This round was independently dispatched
under the working name "R-130" before a concurrent session's own R-130
(`hedge_experts`'s Hedge combinator, entry above) landed on `main` mid-round.
Discovered via a rejected non-fast-forward push; resolved by merging the
concurrent session's `main` and renaming every file in this round from
`r130_*` to `r131_*` (`experiments/r131_shared.py`,
`experiments/r131_conservative_turnover_band.py`,
`experiments/r131_novel_turnover_throttle.py`) before either implementing

flagged the resulting file-content race (the shared pre-registration file
transiently reverting to the concurrent session's own R-130 content mid-run)
rather than silently proceeding on the wrong pre-registration or silently
"fixing" it themselves — exactly the caution this project's own parallel-branch
rules ask for. The operator independently re-ran both branches' Step-0
wiring self-test and causal-truncation probe after the rename, from a clean
shell, and reproduced the conservative branch's probe value bit-for-bit
(18868.799958) confirming the rename did not alter either branch's frozen
mechanism.

**What was done.** `experiments/r131_shared.py` (frozen pre-registration,
splits, market specs, `TURNOVER_UPPER`/`OVERRIDE_MULT`/`ETA`/`LAMBDA_MAX`
constants, `STRESS_EPISODES`, shared `b1_signal`/`trailing_turnover_ewm`/

SIZE/ERR/COST family (R-109...R-130): PROMOTE-candidate only if the

B4 (ETH, full, both markets) AND B5 (0.40% fee) all pass; B2 (drawdown)
diagnostic only. **Conservative** (`experiments/r131_conservative_turnover_band.py`):
a hard defer once trailing turnover reaches `TURNOVER_UPPER`, with an
override that never blocks a full de-risking exit or a move exceeding
`OVERRIDE_MULT * TURNOVER_UPPER`. One legitimate step-3 bug found and fixed
before any inner-validation number was read (disclosed, not selected on):
the first "pending rebalance" trigger compared live
`position*close/equity` to `desired` at a 1e-9 tolerance, firing on ~66% of
*all* bars from ordinary price drift rather than genuine v4 re-target
decisions; fixed to trigger exactly on v4's own `|target[i]-target[i-1]| >
1e-9`, with an `owed` flag persisting a deferred move across bars. **Novel**
(`experiments/r131_novel_turnover_throttle.py`): an online dual-variable
throttle, `lambda_{t+1} = clip(lambda_t + ETA*(turnover_ewm_t -
TURNOVER_UPPER), 0, LAMBDA_MAX)`, shrinking each pending rebalance by
`1/(1+lambda_t)`. **Configurations evaluated: 29 total** (conservative: 1
causal probe + 1 A2 + 4 B1 + 4 B3 + 1 B4 + 2 B5 = 13; novel: 4 B1 + 8 B3 + 2
B4 + 2 B5 = 16, reusing the B1 full-inner-spot run for its causal probe/A2
per its own accounting).

**Verdict.** **NEGATIVE, both branches. Decision rule did not move** —

### R-130 · 08-25 · NEGATIVE (both branches) — moving `hedge_experts`'s cost mechanism from a downstream no-trade band (R-128, R-129: 4/4 constructions failed) INTO the Hedge combinator itself: a lazy-update L1 weight-shrinkage penalty (conservative, Das/Johnson/Banerjee 2013) and a commission-avoidant online-learning wrapper (novel, Uziel & El-Yaniv 2016); the novel branch's apparent partial pass (BTC+ETH spot significant, futures directionally consistent, no BTC/ETH inversion) does not survive independent skeptic ablation — it is a re-derivation of R-64's already-closed Gârleanu-Pedersen smooth trading rate, riding on the broker deadband R-66/B-29 already found "cannot be evaluated honestly," with a mechanism measurably inert to the reward channel it exists to test

**Direction.** Off-backlog (still only B-06, unchanged since R-110). R-128 and R-129 both bolted a Kelly-quadratic-cost no-trade band (Constantinides 1986; Davis & Norman 1990) onto `hedge_experts`'s OUTPUT — R-128 on the single already-blended signal (fixed and adaptive horizon), R-129 on ten raw pre-blend experts or three bucket sub-blends — four constructions, four application points, 0 promoted, R-129's own closing line naming the untested alternative verbatim: "a future attempt on this object needs a cost model outside the Kelly-quadratic-cost family entirely, not a third application point of the same algebra." This round takes that literally: both branches modify or wrap the Hedge weight-update recursion itself (`logw`/`p` inside `HedgeExperts.prepare()`), which R-128/R-129 both left completely untouched, gating only what happened after `p` was already computed. **Attacks COST** — `hedge_experts` pays fees on every re-target and its own weight recursion updates unconditionally every bar with zero cost-awareness baked into it. Literature (WebSearch, this session, before either branch was written): Das, P., Johnson, N., & Banerjee, A. (2013), "Online Lazy Updates for Portfolio Selection with Transaction Costs," *AAAI* 27(1), 202–208 — a primal-dual proximal/lazy-update mechanism that regularizes the weight-update step itself by the transaction cost it would incur (conservative branch). Uziel, G., & El-Yaniv, R. (2016), "Online Learning of Commission Avoidant Portfolio Ensembles," arXiv:1605.00788 — an ensemble meta-algorithm with a logarithmic regret bound relative to commission-oblivious base algorithms, wrapping (rather than modifying) the base combinator (novel branch). Non-duplicate of R-128/R-129 (different application point: inside vs. after the combinator) and of any single-asset `kelly_regime_v4` SIZE/ERR/INFO round (different object). Failure modes pre-registered before either branch wrote code: (1) for the conservative branch, damping the Hedge weight vector `p` might not propagate to fewer re-targets of the traded signal `x = p @ a` if `p`'s own residual movement still crosses the broker's 5% deadband; (2) for the novel branch, the commission-avoidance meta-layer could collapse into something functionally indistinguishable from a band on the output — the same closed axis in different clothing — which the branch was explicitly asked to check for directly, not merely assert against; (3) the standing six-plus-instance BTC-pass/ETH-invert prior.

**What was done.** Two agents worked disjoint files against a common brief (no operator-authored shared harness this round — each branch built its own data/split/baseline plumbing to the same specification, `INNER_TRAIN_START=2017-01-01`, `INNER_VAL_END=2022-12-31`, `OOS_START=2023-01-01` never read by either): `experiments/r130_shared.py` + `experiments/r130_conservative_lazy_hedge.py` (conservative), `experiments/r130_novel_commission_avoidant.py` (novel). Both ran the R-128/R-129 convention battery against frozen `hedge_experts` (paired bootstrap via `tradebot.inference`, both markets, full-inner and inner-validation): B1 (Δ-Sharpe vs. baseline), B3 (a parameter-multiplier plateau sweep, 0.5/1/2/4×), B4 (pre-registered falsification: does the sign replicate on ETH spot via `load_coinbase_eth_spot`), B5 (0.40% fee tier), plus a causal-truncation probe and `pytest tests/test_causality_strict.py`. **Conservative** (`CAPEHedge`'s sibling — entrywise soft-threshold `S_α(v)=sign(v)·max(|v|-α,0)`, α=`fee_rate`, applied to the proposed change in `p` each bar before renormalizing onto the simplex; a disclosed simplification of the paper's L2/ADMM machinery onto Hedge's own entropic softmax update, since the two geometries don't map onto each other 1:1): **24 configurations** (8 B1 + 5 B3 + 4 B4 + 4 B5 + 2 truncation + 1 weight-level diagnostic). **Novel** (`CAPEHedge` — `hedge_experts`'s frozen blend treated as one commission-oblivious base algorithm, paired with an artificial "stay" expert equal to the strategy's own last-held target; a scalar AdaGrad/ONS update learns a mixing weight `w_t∈[0,1]` on realized fee-net reward, `x_t = w_t·hedge_target_t + (1-w_t)·held_t`; regularization strength λ calibrated 100× down from a first guess — `hedge_experts`'s own internal `fee_rate` — to restore interior `w_t` occupancy at 5-minute cadence, disclosed as a scale sanity check rather than a fit to Sharpe): **33 configurations** (27 reported + 6 discarded from the initial mis-scaled λ). Because the novel branch's own report claimed a genuine partial pass — the first candidate on this object in three rounds to clear more than one gate, and the first anywhere in six-plus rounds of this project's history to NOT invert sign on ETH — this project's own "an independent skeptic re-runs each surviving claim before it is believed" rule was invoked (the conservative branch's clean, decisive rejection did not warrant one; **dispatch a skeptic only after the primary reports ≥1 evaluated configuration**, satisfied by both). The skeptic re-ran the novel branch's own script from a clean shell, then built its own ablation harness (`experiments/r130_novel_skeptic_check.py`): a `FixedWHedge` constant-`w` control (identity-verified at `w=1.0` against the unmodified baseline), three reward-channel ablations (`r:=0`, `r:=-r`, a deliberate one-bar-lookahead `r:=`next-bar-return, the last purely diagnostic), a decision-level tamper/peeker causal probe with a working positive control, an extended λ sweep to 1024×, and a direct fixed-`w` sweep — **71 net new configurations** (98 total backtest executions, 27 of which duplicate the primary's own already-counted battery bit-for-bit). **Total configurations evaluated this round, across all branches and the skeptic: 128** (24 + 33 + 71).

**Result.** **Conservative: REJECT, decisively, before ETH is even reached.** B1 negative on all 4 cells (spot full `d_sharpe=-1.080` CI `[-1.449,-0.763]`, spot val `-1.538` CI `[-2.080,-0.969]`, futures full `-0.611` CI `[-0.901,-0.382]`, futures val `-0.525` CI `[-1.065,+0.043]`) — 3 of 4 CIs exclude zero on the losing side. B3 is a plateau of monotonically *worsening* harm (0.5×→4× λ: `-0.854`→`-6.468`), not a peak — sign-consistent but consistently wrong-signed. B4: ETH spot replicates the *negative* sign (full `-0.986` CI `[-1.244,-0.761]`, val `-1.257` CI `[-1.750,-0.871]`) — for once this construction doesn't even get the usual BTC-pass/ETH-invert signature; it fails outright on both assets. B5 negative at 0.40% fee (spot significant `-3.851` CI `[-5.177,-2.563]`; futures directionally negative, CI includes zero). Causal-truncation PASS (bit-identical). Diagnosed mechanism: the shrinkage genuinely damps `p`'s own L1 churn (~47% reduction at full scale, 630K bars) but `p` still moves on 100.0% of bars (never fully zeroed at N=10), and this reduced weight-vector churn does not propagate to fewer re-targets of the traded signal — trade count came out **higher** than baseline in every cell, confirming pre-registered failure mode #1. **Novel: the primary's own reported partial pass does NOT survive skeptic audit — NOT CONFIRMED, and the branch is now REJECT.** The skeptic found no lookahead (a tamper/peeker probe with a working positive control cleanly distinguishes 0/32,500 real perturbed decisions from the deliberate peeker's 1/32,500) and reproduced every headline number bit-for-bit from a clean shell across three bootstrap seeds. But the mechanism the branch exists to test is **measurably inert**: setting `r:=0` — deleting the entire realized-reward channel from the gradient — reproduces the headline numbers to within ±0.001 (BTC spot full-inner `+0.062`→`+0.062`; ETH spot `+0.092`→`+0.091`; 0.40%-fee spot `+0.553`→`+0.552`), and inverting the reward or giving it a deliberate one-bar lookahead changes nothing either. The AdaGrad accumulator `A_t` never meaningfully leaves its seed (`1.0000→1.0089` over 630K bars, so there is no adaptive step size and no logarithmic-regret guarantee in play); `w_t` is instead a near-deterministic annealing decay (`mean|Δw|≈6.4e-7`/bar, 88% net downward drift, effective EMA half-life ≈1.19 bars ≈ 6 minutes). A `FixedWHedge` control — the identical played rule with `w` held CONSTANT, no gradient, no λ, no learning at all — is statistically indistinguishable from the candidate (daily-return correlation 0.9986–0.9996 across cells, `|Δd_sharpe|≤0.030`) and **beats it in 4 of 7 audited cells**, including both headline spot cells and ETH. Two additional hygiene defects in the primary's own reported evidence, found by the skeptic: the causal-truncation probe was vacuous (`run_period` hands the "full" and "truncated" arms an *identical* pre-sliced frame in this construction — verified `.equals()==True` — so the reported PASS would hold for a strategy with perfect foresight too), and the cited `pytest tests/test_causality_strict.py` 51-passed does not cover `CAPEHedge` at all (it is not `@register`-ed, and both tests parametrize only over `available_strategies()`). Once `w` is understood as near-constant, `x_t = w·Σ_k(1-w)^k·g_{t-k}` unrolls to Gârleanu & Pedersen (2013) smooth partial adjustment at trade rate `a=w` — an object this project's own section C (R-64 novel, 376 configurations) already closed under a proportional fee: *"do not re-try a smooth trading rate under a proportional fee at all."* And R-64's own companion finding ("the minimum-step filter does all the work") reproduces exactly here: of 138,616 `order_target` calls the candidate emits, **96.8% are absorbed by `broker.REBALANCE_DEADBAND`** — the identical situation R-66/B-29 named as "cannot be evaluated honestly until a minimum-step rule lives in the strategy rather than in the broker," now confirmed on a second object (`hedge_experts`, not just `kelly_regime_v4`-family constructions). The B3 sweep is not a plateau but a monotone ramp with no interior optimum: extended past the primary's 4× cap, `d_sharpe` climbs to `+0.999` at 256×λ — the winning cell makes 3 trades in two years and is the only configuration ending above the $1,000 start — and every well-scoring cell is exactly the `w→0` degeneracy λ was calibrated to avoid. The underlying fact being measured throughout is that frozen `hedge_experts` loses money on 2021–2022 inner-validation ($594 from $1,000 at 0.10% fees, $220 at 0.40%), so *any* monotone turnover suppressant improves the point estimate — a fixed-α EMA does it at least as well as the "learned" version, with no gradient signal contributing anything. On futures, no cell of either branch or the skeptic's ablations ever hits the engine's liquidation path (`liquidated==False` throughout, all arms, all cells) — the near-zero terminal balances (as low as $1.47–$139 from $1,000 at 5× leverage) are real path outcomes, not a bootstrap artifact from a degenerate zero-variance tail, and the futures full-inner negative point estimate is stable across every one of the skeptic's ablations (significant on the losing side, CI `[-0.159,-0.001]`, under the `r:=-r` variant).

**Verdict.** **NEGATIVE, both branches.** Lesson: a genuinely new *application point* for a cost mechanism (inside the combinator, not after it) is not automatically a genuinely new *mechanism* — the novel branch's meta-algorithm, once its learning signal is ablated away, reduces to a construction (smooth trading rate under proportional cost) and an evaluability defect (broker-deadband absorption) this project had already closed on a different object three years and dozens of rounds ago; the "not a duplicate of" check in a pre-registration needs to include what a mechanism reduces to under its own parameter limits, not only what it is named after. Second lesson, procedural: the skeptic-verification step this project's own parallel-round rules require is not a formality here — it reversed a genuinely close, well-documented, multi-gate "partial pass" into a decisive reject, on evidence (a single-line reward-deletion ablation) the primary branch's own falsification battery had no gate designed to catch. **Holdout counter: unchanged, +0 added.** No holdout was consulted by either branch or the skeptic (max timestamp read anywhere this round: `2022-12-31 23:55:00+00:00`, verified) — the novel branch's apparent pass was falsified by ablation *before* a pre-registered holdout decision rule was ever written, exactly the "look-once" discipline this project's routine exists to protect: better to not spend the consultation than to spend it on a candidate that does not survive its own skeptic review. Decision rule did not move (none was pre-registered against the holdout this round). Next step: `hedge_experts`'s own COST axis is now closed across three structurally distinct families and every combinator application point this project's framework can construct for it — Kelly-quadratic-cost bands (R-128, R-129: 4 constructions, output-level and pre-blend), lazy-update weight shrinkage (this round, conservative: inside the combinator), and commission-avoidant/smooth-trading-rate online learning (this round, novel: wrapping the combinator) — a future attempt on this object's turnover needs a mechanism that isn't reducible to "trade less, monotonically" under this project's proportional-fee broker, which is a materially harder bar than any of the seven constructions tried so far have cleared, or should vary something about `hedge_experts` other than its re-target/cost rule (its EXPERT COMPOSITION, e.g., has never been touched by any two-branch round).

### R-129 · 08-25 · NEGATIVE (both branches) — moving `hedge_experts`'s EV-derived rebalance band from the already-blended output (R-128, NEGATIVE) to BEFORE the blend: ten per-expert bands (conservative) and three per-timescale-bucket bands (novel), both failing B1 and B5 despite passing B3/B4, with R-128's own two pre-registered failure modes confirmed in opposite, informative ways on the two branches

**Direction.** Off-backlog (still only B-06, unchanged since R-110). R-128 tried ONE EV-derived no-trade band (the algebra that earned `kelly_regime_ev` a real promotion: Constantinides 1986; Davis & Norman 1990) on `hedge_experts`'s already-Hedge-blended output signal, at a fixed and an adaptive horizon — both NEGATIVE, on the exact risk R-128 pre-registered: the algebra assumes one homogeneous stationary bet, but `hedge_experts` blends ten experts across four timescales. R-128's own closing line named the untested alternative verbatim: "a band construction that does not assume one homogeneous target (e.g. a per-expert or per-timescale no-trade rule rather than one band on the already-blended output)." This round tests exactly that split, one branch per named alternative. **Attacks COST.** New literature grounding this session (WebSearch, before either branch was written): Ekren, Liu & Muhle-Karbe (2018), "Optimal Rebalancing Frequencies for Multidimensional Portfolios", *Mathematics and Financial Economics* 12(1), 1-24 (arXiv:1510.05097) — the multivariate extension of the classical single-asset no-trade-region result, cited for the general shape of the question (does a jointly optimal multi-signal no-trade region look like several per-object bands or one pooled band — the paper's own answer is "neither trivially, the joint region is generally wider than either"), not reproduced (its own HJB stochastic-control solution needs correlated-diffusion machinery this project's causal bar-by-bar simulator cannot evaluate; both branches instead apply `kelly_regime_ev`'s already-validated closed-form heuristic per-object/per-bucket). Non-duplicate of R-128 (bands the ONE already-blended signal, never anything before the blend, and uses a fitted/measured horizon, not a structural one), of `kelly_regime_ev` (single homogeneous vote, not a multi-expert blend), of the `xsmom_entry_band` panel-selection line (B-29 through B-41, a different engine/object), and of R-126 (`champions_council`'s cross-strategy allocation weights, not one strategy's own pre-blend construction). Five failure modes pre-registered before any code ran, all in `experiments/r129_shared.py`'s frozen module docstring: (1) Hedge's multiplicative weights update every bar with no hysteresis of their own, so damping the raw inputs might not stop the final blend from moving regardless; (2) very-short-horizon inputs get very WIDE bands by the `2*fee/(H*sigma^2)` algebra (short horizon → small denominator term → large threshold), which could clip to `MAX_BAND=1.0` and freeze near-permanently; (3) the standing six-plus-instance BTC-pass/ETH-invert prior; (4) a band wide enough to matter could reproduce the LAG failure measured in all 11 `kelly_regime_v4` regime-timing mechanisms; (5) the novel branch's bucket boundaries are a structural judgement call, not fit — a real, disclosed limit of testing one partition.

**What was done.** `experiments/r129_shared.py` (operator-authored, frozen before either branch was dispatched): the full pre-registration above, ten structural per-expert horizons (`EXPERT_HORIZON_DAYS`, derived from each expert's own lookback/decay construction in `HedgeExperts._experts` — e.g. 0.0035d for 1-bar reversion up to 7.0d nominal for the two constant experts — never fit to a return), a frozen three-way bucket assignment (`EXPERT_BUCKET`: FAST = 1h/6h momentum + MACD + RSI + 1-bar reversion, SLOW = 1d/1w momentum + Donchian, STATIC = always-flat + buy-and-hold) with each bucket's horizon the structural median of its members', `MIN_BAND=0.02`/`MAX_BAND=1.0` (`kelly_regime_ev`'s/R-128's own literal defaults), and — critical after R-128's own post-hoc unit bug — a binding **Implementation note** specifying the exact causal state-machine both branches had to build: `prepare()` stays fully market-independent (emits the raw 10-expert matrix and raw 10-weight matrix as plain columns, reusing `HedgeExperts._experts()` and its `g`/`logw`/`p` loop verbatim); `on_bar()` tracks per-expert/per-bucket "held" values as INSTANCE state (no broker-side equivalent exists for a sub-position), initialized once at the first `on_bar` call to that bar's own live value (a disclosed, bounded cold-start convention, 0.6% of inner-train bars); the band is computed in fraction-of-max-leverage units (dividing by `ctx.market.leverage`) and orders are placed via `ctx.order_target` throughout — pre-empting R-128's exact unit mismatch (comparing a fraction-of-leverage signal against a notional-multiple `current`, routed through `order_notional`) by construction rather than discovering it post-hoc. Two independent agents built `experiments/r129_conservative_per_expert_band.py` (ten independent per-expert bands, weight applied live at blend time so only the raw expert values are damped) and `experiments/r129_novel_bucket_band.py` (three bucket sub-blends, each independently banded, summed for the final target) from the frozen shared module; neither is `@register`ed. Both ran the identical B1 (BTC spot+futures, full period + inner-validation, paired-bootstrap vs unmodified `hedge_experts`)/B3 (a single multiplier 0.5/1/2/4x scaling every horizon in the branch's own construction simultaneously, FUTURES inner-validation)/B4 (ETH spot falsification, inner-validation, primary config)/B5 (0.40% fee tier, same 4 B1 cells) battery R-125 through R-128 established, plus a diagnostic per-expert/per-bucket re-target count checking failure modes 1-2 directly rather than assuming them. **Configs evaluated: 28 total** (14 conservative + 14 novel: 1 causal probe + 4 B1 + 4 B3 + 1 B4 + 4 B5, each). `pytest tests/test_causality_strict.py -q`: 51 passed, both branches. **Decision rule, pre-registered, unchanged after seeing any number:** PROMOTE-candidate only if the causal probe AND B1 (all 4 cells) AND B3 (>=3/4 same-signed) AND B4 (sign replicates) AND B5 (no flip) all pass.

**Result.** **Both branches NEGATIVE on the same two gates (B1, B5), via different mechanisms.** **Conservative (per-expert):** causal probe PASS (16450.0409 both runs, bit-identical); **B1 FAILS 0/4** — spot full `d_sharpe=+0.0359` CI `[-0.099,+0.325]`, spot val `+0.1083` CI `[-0.085,+0.180]`, futures full `-0.1470` CI `[-4.454,-1.412]` (excludes zero on the losing side), futures val `-0.0367` CI `[-0.827,+0.204]` — no cell clears the `+0.2` floor, a positive CI, or a `>=5pp` drawdown improvement; B3 passes but its 4/4 majority sign is **negative** throughout (`-0.035` to `-0.093` across the 0.5x-4x sweep) — a consistent, not merely non-significant, futures-side loss; B4 passes weakly (ETH `+0.0536` CI `[-0.071,+0.170]`, same sign as BTC's `+1`, CI straddles zero); **B5 FAILS** — futures inner-validation flips sign (`-0.0367` → `+0.0897`) at the 0.40% tier. Diagnostic: candidate trade count vs baseline is 0.57x/0.62x/0.77x/1.11x across the four B1 cells (spot full/val, futures full/val) — turnover falls only modestly and **rises** on futures inner-validation, confirming **failure mode #1**: `x = weight @ held` recomputes every bar from the live, unbanded Hedge weights, so the blended output keeps moving even when every individual `held[j]` is frozen. Per-expert re-target table (628,220 on_bar calls, BTC spot full period) confirms **failure mode #2**: expert 6 (1-bar reversion, the shortest structural horizon at 0.0035d) re-targets **zero** times over the whole window — frozen at cold-start — and expert 4 (MACD, 0.090d) re-targets 4 times; the four momentum experts (0.042d-7.0d) and RSI/Donchian re-target at meaningfully higher rates (0.2%-4.0% of bars). **Novel (per-timescale-bucket):** causal probe PASS (13014.7519 both runs, bit-identical); **B1 FAILS — only 1 of 4 cells clears** (spot val, `d_sharpe=+0.3906`, clears on the `+0.2` floor alone; spot full `+0.1099` CI `[-0.334,+0.901]`, futures full `-0.0932` CI `[-3.374,+0.401]`, futures val `+0.1523` CI `[-0.533,+1.131]` all fail every OR-clause) — note this is **1/4, not the 2/4 the implementing agent's own chat summary claimed**; the operator's independent read of the agent's own `r129_novel_report.md` table found the discrepancy (row-by-row: only spot-val's `clears?` cell reads True) before this entry was written, a small but real instance of this project's own "trust the artifact, not the recap" discipline; B3 passes cleanly, 4/4 positive across the sweep; B4 passes more substantively than the conservative branch (ETH `+0.3206` CI `[-0.100,+0.635]`, same sign as BTC's `+1`); **B5 FAILS** — futures full-period flips sign (`-0.0932` → `+0.3331`) at the 0.40% tier. Diagnostic: candidate trade count vs baseline is 56/1444, 18/451, 547/3002, 244/662 (spot full/val, futures full/val) — turnover falls hard in every cell, **failure mode #1 did NOT materialize** on this branch, the opposite finding from conservative. Per-bucket re-target table (631,008 bars) instead delivers the sharpest instance yet of **failure mode #2**: the FAST bucket (5 of 10 experts — 1h/6h momentum, MACD, RSI, 1-bar reversion) re-targets **zero** times across the entire full period, permanently frozen at its cold-start value, while SLOW (333 re-targets) and STATIC (592) both move meaningfully more — the reverse of the naive expectation that the two structurally-constant STATIC experts would freeze most (STATIC's sub-blend is carried entirely by the buy-and-hold expert's own Hedge weight, which drifts enough relative to STATIC's comparatively tight ~7-day band to re-target more often than the "faster" bucket does). **Skeptic reproduction, both branches, complete:** the operator independently re-ran both scripts end-to-end from a clean shell (599s conservative, 528s novel) and every printed number matched the implementing agents' own reports bit-for-bit — both causal-truncation probes (16450.0409, 13014.7519), all 8 B1 cells, all 8 B3 sweep points, both B4 cells, all 8 B5 cells, every per-expert/per-bucket re-target count, and both `pytest tests/test_causality_strict.py` runs (51 passed, 46.58s/47.80s conservative, 47.11s/47.17s novel — timing is the only non-identical figure anywhere in either reproduction). This includes independent confirmation of the 1-of-4 (not 2-of-4) novel B1 count above.

**Verdict.** **NEGATIVE, both branches. Decision rule did not move** — applied exactly as frozen in `experiments/r129_shared.py`, before either branch was dispatched, unrelaxed by any number seen afterward. **The substantive finding, and it is the round's most reusable one: turnover control and mechanism-preservation trade off against banding granularity, in a specific, now-measured direction.** Ten independent per-expert bands (fine-grained) barely dent turnover — Hedge's own continuous weight churn routes around per-input damping almost entirely, exactly failure mode #1 — while three per-timescale-bucket bands (coarse-grained) cut turnover hard, but at the cost of a sharper version of failure mode #2: an entire five-member bucket, not just one short-horizon expert, permanently silenced for the whole backtest. Neither granularity threads the needle R-128's own closing line hoped a pre-blend construction might: the fine-grained version doesn't control cost, the coarse-grained version controls cost by amputating half the ensemble rather than by timing trades better, and both still fail B1 (no cell clears convincingly) and B5 (a sign flip at the realistic fee tier) regardless. **This closes the pre-blend-banding axis for `hedge_experts`'s own re-target rule**: blended-output (R-128, two horizon constructions) and pre-blend (this round, two granularities) are now both tried, 4 constructions total, 0 promoted, and R-128's own two candidate remedies for its structural-mismatch diagnosis have both been exhausted. **The methodological finding:** an implementing agent's own prose summary of its results can disagree with its own generated report even when the underlying computation and battery are correct (the novel branch's 1-of-4-vs-claimed-2-of-4 B1 count) — worth a habitual cross-check of the artifact against the recap on every future round, not just the numbers the recap chooses to lead with. **Holdout counter: +0** on top of R-128's ~698 (unchanged); running program-level total remains **~698** — neither branch, nor either agent's run, nor the operator's independent re-run, ever read a bar dated 2023-01-01 or later (max timestamp `2022-12-31 23:55:00+00:00` throughout). **Next step:** `hedge_experts`'s own re-target rule is now closed across both axes of variation this project's framework can construct for it (WHERE the band applies — blended output vs. pre-blend — and, within pre-blend, WHAT granularity); a future session preferring this object needs a mechanism outside the Kelly-quadratic-cost band family entirely (e.g. a genuinely different cost model, not a different application point of the same one) or should treat this as a second, sharper data point (after R-126) that COST-axis fixes proven on `kelly_regime_v4`'s single homogeneous bet do not transfer to this project's multi-expert/multi-strategy objects by varying only where or how coarsely the same algebra is applied. The ranked backlog otherwise remains as R-128 left it: empty of anything but **B-06** (forward paper-trading, already running unattended).

### R-128 · 08-25 · NEGATIVE (both branches, one bug found and fixed mid-round) — an EV-derived no-trade band, fixed (conservative) and adaptive-horizon (novel), transplanted from `kelly_regime_ev` onto `hedge_experts`'s own re-target rule; a self-inflicted exposure-unit bug inflated both branches' first-run futures numbers into a false PROMOTE-candidate, corrected before any verdict was recorded

**Direction.** Off-backlog (the ranked list has held only B-06 since R-110; the single-asset `kelly_regime_v4` axis — 19+ INFO signals, 28+ SIZE attempts, ERR across 5 notions of uncertainty, 11 regime-timing mechanisms, 4 N≈3 procedures — and `champions_council`'s own allocation mechanism (R-126) are both closed; R-127 diagnosed the recurring BTC/ETH signature rather than testing a new mechanism). This round picked a third object never varied by any of the prior 127 rounds: `hedge_experts` (L-09), whose own `on_bar` re-targets its Hedge-blended position whenever `abs(x-pos) > hysteresis` for a FIXED `hysteresis=0.05` — the same class of hand-set, never-derived threshold `kelly_regime`'s original 10% deadband was, before `kelly_regime_ev` derived `band = 2*fee/(H*sigma^2)` from Kelly quadratic-growth-cost-vs-linear-fee algebra (Constantinides 1986; Davis & Norman 1990) and shipped it (finding 7, `docs/RESEARCH.md`). **Attacks COST.** Grep-confirmed non-duplicate: `hedge_experts` appears in only 6 `docs/LEDGER.md` lines pre-round, none about its hysteresis/deadband mechanism; not a duplicate of the `xsmom_entry_band` multi-asset entry/exit-band line (B-29 through B-41, R-64–R-69, R-108 — a cross-sectional panel-selection rule on a different engine) or of R-126 (`champions_council`'s cross-strategy allocation weights, not a single strategy's own re-target rule). Conservative branch: the literal `kelly_regime_ev` transplant, `H` a single frozen constant (`HORIZON_DAYS_FROZEN=1.294` days, `hedge_experts`'s own current fixed-hysteresis fill spacing on inner-train, pooled across markets). Novel branch: the same algebra with `H_t` computed online from a causal EWM lag-1 autocorrelation of the blend signal `x` itself (an implied AR(1) persistence horizon) — the "state-dependence of the horizon" axis R-89 finding 11 named as one of three legitimate single-instrument variation axes (Levine & Pedersen 2016) and did not itself take; not a re-run of B-40 (which made the *vote's* weights state-dependent via a discrete 4-state classifier, not the *band's* horizon via a continuous persistence estimate). Named failure modes, pre-registered before any code ran (all in `experiments/r128_shared.py`'s frozen docstring): the fixed 0.05 might already be a coincidental near-optimum (null result); a seventh BTC-pass/ETH-invert construction (B4 exists to catch this); the Kelly algebra assumes one homogeneous stationary bet, and `hedge_experts` blends ten experts across four timescales (the sharpest named risk); a wide-enough band could reproduce the LAG failure this project has measured in every regime-timing mechanism on `kelly_regime_v4`.

**What was done.** `experiments/r128_shared.py` (operator-authored, frozen before either branch was dispatched): splits, `HORIZON_DAYS_FROZEN`, the B1/B4 battery primitives, and the full pre-registration (mechanism, non-duplicate argument, named failure modes, decision rule) — matching the B1/B3/B4/B5 convention this SIZE/ERR/COST research programme has used since R-59/R-64. Two independent agents built `experiments/r128_conservative_ev_band.py` and `experiments/r128_novel_adaptive_band.py`, each subclassing `HedgeExperts` and reusing `HedgeExperts._experts()` verbatim so only the re-target rule changes; neither is `@register`ed. **A bug was found on operator review of the first-run reports, before any verdict was accepted**, per ROUTINE.md's own "going back to fix a bug is fine and always was" allowance: both branches' task instructions (mine, as round designer) directed them to copy `kelly_regime_ev.on_bar`'s body literally, which compares `hedge_experts`'s own blend `x` — already in "fraction of this market's max leverage" units, the convention its own experts and its original `ctx.order_target` call use — against `current = position*close/equity`, a NOTIONAL-MULTIPLE (ranges to ±5 on 5x futures), then places orders via `ctx.order_notional` (leverage-invariant) instead of `hedge_experts`'s native `ctx.order_target` (leverage-scaled). The two conventions coincide on spot (leverage=1) and diverge on futures, where the bug silently capped both candidates near 1x equity notional regardless of the real 5x cap — an EXPOSURE-LEVEL artifact, exactly the R-33 trap ("holding less draws down less; that is arithmetic, not evidence") this project's ledger names repeatedly, not a rebalance-timing effect. The novel branch independently surfaced a second, unrelated bug during its own report-writing: `RHO_MAX=0.98` and `H_MIN_DAYS=0.25` were mutually inconsistent (the maximum unclipped `H_t` reachable at `rho=0.98` is ≈0.172 days, always below the 0.25-day floor), so its adaptive `H_t` was mathematically pinned to the floor on every bar in every configuration — the mechanism that round existed to test never varied. Both fixes applied by the operator (algebra: `band` gains one extra `/leverage` factor in fraction-of-leverage units; `RHO_MAX` raised to 0.999) and the full battery re-run for both branches; the SPOT-only and ETH-only cells are numerically unaffected by the leverage fix (leverage=1 throughout) but the novel branch's whole battery was re-run regardless since the `RHO_MAX` fix changes every cell's `H_t` path. Neither branch touched a bar at or after `OOS_START=2023-01-01` in either the first or corrected run. **Configs evaluated: 28 total** (14 conservative + 14 novel; identical count before and after the fix — the correction changed the code, not the battery design). `pytest tests/test_causality_strict.py`: 51 passed, both branches, both before and after the fix.

**Result.** **Conservative, corrected: B1 FAILS, B3 passes (3/4, now negative-leaning), B4 PASSES (weakly), B5 FAILS.** Spot is genuinely positive and unaffected by the fix: full-period `d_sharpe=+0.045` (via an 8.8pp drawdown improvement, boot CI `[-0.672,+0.759]`), inner-validation `d_sharpe=+0.586` (CI `[-0.046,+0.741]`) — neither individually significant but consistent in sign, and ETH spot `d_sharpe=+0.107` (CI `[-0.357,+0.581]`) matches BTC's sign, satisfying B4, though an order of magnitude smaller. Futures inverts once corrected: full-period `d_sharpe=-0.209` with a bootstrap CI `[-5.108,-2.025]` that excludes zero entirely on the losing side — the single most decisive number this round produced — and inner-validation `d_sharpe=-0.108`; both drawdowns are now *worse* than baseline, and two of the four B5 (0.40% fee) cells flip sign. **Novel, corrected: B1 FAILS, B3 "passes" (4/4 same-signed, now genuinely and consistently negative), B4 FAILS (sign inverts), B5 FAILS.** The `RHO_MAX` fix confirmed the mechanism now genuinely varies (`H_t` median 1.77 days, p5/p95 0.80/3.47 days, only 0.3% of bars at the floor, vs. 100% pinned before the fix) — this is an informative NEGATIVE, not an untested one. Futures-full is again the sharpest number in the round: `d_sharpe=-0.146`, CI `[-4.149,-1.174]`, excludes zero. **B4 fails outright**: ETH spot `d_sharpe=-0.124` against BTC spot-val's `+0.571` — a genuine sign inversion, the **seventh** distinct mechanism/object on this project to pass part of a BTC gate and invert on ETH (joining R-109, R-113, R-115-conservative, R-125-conservative, R-126 both branches), though this round is mixed rather than a clean seventh notch: the conservative branch's ETH cell did *not* invert (B4 passed there), only the novel branch's did. B5 fails on 3 of 4 cells (spot-full, futures-full, futures-val all flip sign at the 0.40% tier). Both branches' first (confounded) run reported a mechanical PROMOTE-candidate verdict on all or nearly all gates — preserved in git history (`3b6d924` and earlier) and in each report's own file, not deleted — which the corrected run reverses on both.

**Verdict.** **NEGATIVE, both branches. Decision rule did not move** — the pre-registered rule was applied exactly as written, before and after the bug fix; nothing was relaxed to rescue either branch, the bug fix corrected an implementation defect (a unit mismatch, a clip-bound inconsistency), not a threshold, per ROUTINE.md's explicit allowance for that distinction. **One-line lesson, two layers.** The substantive finding: this round's own sharpest pre-registered risk was right — the Kelly quadratic-cost-vs-linear-fee algebra that earned a real promotion on `kelly_regime_v4`'s single, roughly homogeneous bet does not transfer to `hedge_experts`'s ten-expert, four-timescale blend; SPOT alone is a genuine, if not individually significant, positive result across both branches, but FUTURES decisively reverses it, and the round's own "both markets" bar was never optional. The methodological finding, arguably the more valuable one: a literal mechanism transplant between two strategies with different native position-sizing conventions (`kelly_regime_v4`'s target is already an equity-notional-multiple; `hedge_experts`'s blend is a fraction of max leverage) is not free — copying working code between objects can silently change what units a comparison is even being made in, and the resulting artifact (both candidates capped near 1x notional on 5x futures, mechanically avoiding `hedge_experts`'s own catastrophic 99.8-99.9% baseline drawdown there) looked, before correction, exactly like a genuine COST-axis win. This is a first-hand instance of the standing rule ("match risk before comparing anything") applying to a *round's own candidate construction*, not just to a benchmark choice — worth carrying into any future round that ports a mechanism between two strategies rather than varying one strategy's own parameter. **Holdout counter: +0** on top of R-127's ~698 (unchanged); running program-level total remains **~698** — neither branch, nor either run, ever read a bar dated 2023-01-01 or later. **Next step:** the `hedge_experts` re-target axis is now closed for the Kelly-quadratic-cost band family specifically (both a fixed and an adaptive horizon tried, both NEGATIVE on futures) — a future session could try a band construction that does not assume one homogeneous target (e.g. a per-expert or per-timescale no-trade rule rather than one band on the already-blended output), or accept this as a second data point (after R-126) that COST-axis fixes proven on `kelly_regime_v4` do not automatically generalize to this project's other strategy objects. The ranked backlog otherwise remains as R-127 left it: empty of anything but **B-06** (forward paper-trading, already running unattended).

### R-127 · 08-25 · METHOD (diagnostic, both branches) — investigating the six-fold BTC-pass/ETH-invert signature itself rather than testing a 7th mechanism: does calendar-window mismatch explain it (no), and do ETH-idiosyncratic events explain it (partially, for the one construction tested)

**Direction.** Off-backlog (still only B-06, unchanged since R-110). Six independent prior constructions across three mechanism axes and two objects (R-109, R-113, R-115-conservative, R-125-conservative, R-126 both branches) have passed this project's B1 gate on BTC and inverted sign on ETH's B4 falsification test, under a convention — comparing BTC and ETH on identical calendar dates, `INNER_VAL = 2021-01-01..2022-12-31` — that ~40 prior rounds reading B4 have never examined. This round is the first to vary the TEST rather than the mechanism, the same "cost the plan, not just the mechanism" move R-33 made on risk-matching, R-57 on cross-asset scope, and R-78 on the forward-trading horizon. **Attacks N≈3** (does BTC's and ETH's regime composition over the same 24 months differ enough to matter) and **ERR** (an unexamined test-construction assumption is a gap in error control independent of any one mechanism). Full non-duplicate argument, citations (Ang & Bekaert 2002; Guidolin & Timmermann 2007 for regime characterization; Rockafellar & Uryasev 2000 and Maillard-Roncalli-Teiletche 2010 reused by citation for R-126's own construction, not re-derived), the single-frozen-window anti-dredging discipline, and the two-stage pre-registration all live in the operator-authored, frozen `experiments/r127_shared.py` module docstring, written before either branch was dispatched as an independent agent.

**What was done.** `experiments/r127_shared.py` (frozen infrastructure, computed once, shared): a 10-statistic regime fingerprint (annualized vol, vol-of-vol, mean return, skew, excess kurtosis, ACF at lags 1/5/20, max drawdown, fraction-positive-days) on calendar-daily log returns, and a scan of 95 candidate 730-day ETH windows (weekly-stepped, spanning ETH's full pre-holdout history 2019-03-14→2022-12-31) each compared to BTC's fixed `INNER_VAL` fingerprint by standardized Euclidean distance — computed and frozen *before* either branch script existed, so neither branch could select a window by its own outcome. **CONSERVATIVE** (`r127_conservative_regime_fingerprint.py`, pure diagnostic, no strategy code): formalizes the pre-registered coarse test (does the calendar window's fingerprint distance exceed the 90th percentile of the 95-candidate null?) and adds two dependency-free (no scipy in this sandbox) two-sample significance tests — a Brown-Forsythe/Levene-type permutation test for equal variance and a two-sample KS permutation test for equal distribution, 20,000 permutations each, seed fixed before either ran — on BTC vs ETH calendar-window daily log returns. **NOVEL** (`r127_novel_event_excision_retest.py`): the window scan's own result (below) made the originally-planned "regime-matched retest" moot before any performance number was touched, so the branch's design pivoted, pre-code, to a finer hypothesis — do brief ETH-idiosyncratic divergence episodes inside the (correctly-matched) window drive the inversion? Re-evaluates R-126 novel's own already-recorded CVaR-budgeted `champions_council` reallocation (no refit, no new mechanism) under three post-hoc excisions of its already-realized daily return series: (a) two structurally-dated, public-record ETH-idiosyncratic event windows with no BTC analogue (Terra/Luna collapse, 2022-05-04..05-18; The Merge, 2022-09-08..09-22 — 30 of 729 days), (b) a data-driven low-BTC/ETH-correlation-day filter (trailing 14-day corr < 0.30, structural threshold, 11 days), (c) their union (41 days, zero overlap between (a) and (b)). **Configs evaluated: 12 total** (8 conservative: 1 coarse-percentile read + 2 significance tests + 1 fingerprint table + 4 robustness-window checks; 4 novel: 1 baseline reproduction + 3 excision paired tests) — no strategy backtest sweep in the conservative branch, no new mechanism fit in the novel branch. Pre-registered decision rule: this round produces no promotable strategy candidate by design (a diagnostic of the B4 convention, not a new mechanism); the deliverable is a documented finding, whichever way the evidence points. No bar at or after `OOS_START = 2023-01-01` was read by either branch.

**Result.** **Coarse hypothesis (conservative): REFUTED, decisively, on the pre-registered criterion.** The calendar-matched ETH window's fingerprint distance sits at the **1.05th percentile** among all 95 candidates — the single closest regime match to BTC's `INNER_VAL`, not the 90th-percentile-or-worse outlier the confound hypothesis needed. `REGIME_MATCHED_ETH_WINDOW == CALENDAR_ETH_WINDOW` exactly; ranks 2–5 sit at percentiles 2.11/3.16/4.21/5.26, a broad contiguous region of good matches rather than a rank-1 fluke. The two supplementary significance tests add a real nuance without contradicting this: BTC and ETH's raw-scale daily-return distributions over `INNER_VAL` do differ significantly (Brown-Forsythe W=33.25, p=0.0000; two-sample KS D=0.0905, p=0.0050; ETH/BTC variance ratio 1.78×) — but the fingerprint distance is a *standardized* metric, so a raw-scale gap large enough to be significant at n=729 can still rank as the best available match if ETH's other 94 candidate windows carry a similarly elevated volatility relative to BTC, which is exactly what ETH's structurally higher realized volatility across its whole pre-holdout history predicts. `ann_vol` and `acf_lag5` jointly explain ~86% of the aggregate squared distance. **Refined hypothesis (novel): CONFIRMED (partial), for the one construction tested.** Excising Terra/Luna + The Merge (30 days, 4.1% of the window) narrows R-126 novel's ETH daily-return `d_sharpe` gap by ~60% (-0.554 → -0.223, clearing this project's own ±0.2 noise floor for "material"); the union with the low-correlation-day filter narrows it ~78% (-0.554 → -0.121); the low-correlation filter alone (zero date overlap with the named events) narrows it only ~18% (to -0.454, inside the noise floor). **No excision flips the sign** — ETH's candidate remains behind `champions_council` in every variant, so the strict B4 sign-replication test still fails after excision, and none of the four paired-bootstrap intervals excludes zero at n=688–729. Step-1 self-check reproduced R-126's own published ETH `d_sharpe=-0.530` to `-0.5302` (diff -0.0002, same sign) before any excision was applied. Both branches' own printed max-timestamp lines read `2022-12-31 23:55:00+00:00`; the operator independently re-ran both scripts from a clean shell (11s conservative, 96s novel) and reproduced every printed number — percentile 1.05, both test statistics and p-values, the full fingerprint table, and all four novel-branch daily-Sharpe/paired-diff rows — bit-for-bit, and independently re-ran `pytest tests/test_causality_strict.py` (51 passed).

**Verdict.** **METHOD — a documented, mixed diagnostic result, no promotable candidate, and both prongs of the round's own falsification test resolved cleanly rather than ambiguously.** The 40-round-old calendar-window B4 convention, examined for the first time, turns out to already be doing the right thing — BTC and ETH's regime composition over `INNER_VAL` is unusually well aligned, not a silent mismatch, because both assets move through the same market-wide crypto cycle (2021 bull, 2022 bear) together. That rules out one specific, previously-unexamined candidate explanation for the six-fold BTC-pass/ETH-invert pattern. It does not explain the pattern itself: the novel branch's finer test finds that a small number of ETH-specific structural days (Terra/Luna, the Merge — 4.1% of the window) account for roughly 60–78% of the *magnitude* of R-126 novel's own gap, genuine and structured evidence that idiosyncratic divergence is doing real work — but a residual, sign-unchanged gap survives even after removing them, so idiosyncratic-episode excision narrows without fully explaining the inversion for this one construction, and neither "the pattern is a data artifact" nor "the window/events explain nothing" is the correct one-line summary. **One-line lesson:** a long-standing test-construction assumption can be worth checking even when ~40 rounds have already relied on it without incident — sometimes the check confirms the convention (window matching) and sometimes it partially explains the puzzle it was aimed at (event excision), and both outcomes are worth having on record rather than assumed. **Holdout counter: +0** on top of R-126's ~698 (unchanged); running program-level total remains **~698** — neither branch, nor the operator's independent re-runs, ever read a bar dated 2023-01-01 or later. **Decision rule did not move**: pre-registered as a no-promotion diagnostic before either branch ran, and neither branch's output changed that framing after the fact. **Next step:** per the novel branch's own closing line, whether idiosyncratic-event excision generalizes is untested on the other five inverting constructions (R-109, R-113, R-115-conservative, R-125-conservative, R-126-conservative) — each would need its own excision battery re-run on its own fitted target, a concrete, cheap, non-duplicate follow-on for a future session preferring to continue this line rather than open a fresh mechanism search. The ranked backlog otherwise remains as R-126 left it: empty of anything but **B-06** (forward paper-trading, already running unattended).

### R-126 · 08-25 · NEGATIVE (both branches) — `champions_council`'s own between-strategy capital allocation (Hedge/multiplicative weights, never varied since its L-08 registration) replaced with Equal Risk Contribution (conservative) and a CVaR-budgeted convex reallocation (novel): the first round to vary a *portfolio-of-strategies* object rather than one strategy's internal vote/scale, and the sixth distinct construction to pass cleanly on BTC and invert on ETH

**Direction.** Off-backlog — the ranked list has held nothing but B-06 since R-110, reconfirmed by R-125's own re-ranking ("`kelly_regime_v4` is close to efficient with respect to the information, error control and parameter-selection procedure available to this project"). Per `docs/ROUTINE.md`'s own instruction ("invent a new direction only when the backlog is empty, fully blocked, or stale"), this round's own Step-0 diligence — a data-file audit (`data/*.csv.gz` columns, looking for any unused field in the committed `perp_metrics`/on-chain/macro files), a `docs/LEDGER.md` grep for every candidate signal or mechanism (SOPR, NUPL, exchange flow, whale ratio, meta-labeling, conformal prediction, Markowitz/Black-Litterman, gradient-boosted meta-labels), and a WebSearch literature pass — confirmed every axis *internal to* `kelly_regime_v4` and the multi-asset panel is closed: 19 INFO-axis attempts, 27+ SIZE-axis attempts (including R-125's own risk-measure substitution, the same session immediately prior to this one), ERR closed across five notions of uncertainty, eleven regime-timing mechanisms, four N≈3 calibration procedures, eleven multi-asset-panel rounds. Rather than force a 20th INFO signal or a 28th internal SIZE variant, this round picked a genuinely different OBJECT: `champions_council` (L-08, 08-14), a Hedge/multiplicative-weights (Freund & Schapire 1997, JCSS; Arora, Hazan & Kale 2012) portfolio across four already-profitable strategies (`kelly_regime`, `hedge_experts`, `replicator_book`, `universal_kelly`) plus buy-and-hold and flat. Grep-confirmed against `docs/LEDGER.md`: no round since its registration has ever varied its allocation mechanism — the only two other mentions of `champions_council` are R-29's blanket 25-strategy holdout sweep and a walk-forward comparison in `scripts/experiment.py`, neither of which touches its Hedge weights.

One sentence: does replacing `champions_council`'s regret-minimizing Hedge allocation across its 6 members with a risk-budgeted allocation that targets the members' *joint risk* directly — Equal Risk Contribution (Maillard, Roncalli & Teiletche 2010, *J. Portfolio Management* 36(4), 60-70) for the conservative branch, a CVaR-budgeted convex reallocation (Rockafellar & Uryasev 2000, *J. Risk* 2(3), 21-41) for the novel branch — beat the incumbent Hedge blend? **Attacks SIZE** — how much capital to allocate, applied for the first time at the *between-strategy portfolio* level rather than inside one strategy's own vote/scale, the axis this project's standing diagnosis credits as "what actually worked." Non-duplicate of R-107 (the same Maillard-Roncalli-Teiletche paper, applied to a panel of six *assets* — BCH/LTC/ETC/DASH/LINK/XTZ — not to `champions_council`'s four-strategy-plus-two-benchmark member set) and of R-125 (CVaR substituted into `kelly_regime_v4`'s own internal `scale`, a scalar leverage multiplier, not a simplex-constrained cross-strategy weight vector solved by convex optimization). Full non-duplicate argument, citations, and the named failure mode — all 6 members are directionally long-biased against the same BTC/ETH price series, so if their daily payoffs are highly cross-correlated both branches risk converging back toward Hedge's own path, or lacking enough effective independent bets to fit a stable weight vector at all — live in the operator-authored, frozen `experiments/r126_shared.py` module docstring, written before either branch was dispatched as an independent agent.

**What was done.** `experiments/r126_shared.py` (operator-authored, frozen before either branch was dispatched): a byte-identical reproduction of `champions_council`'s own 6-member signal matrix (`member_signal_matrix`) and a shared, fully causal daily payoff matrix per member (`member_daily_payoffs`, `a[i-1]*r[i]` resampled to one row per UTC calendar day, the "daily not 5m-bar" convention `tradebot.inference` uses throughout), a Step-0 non-degeneracy gate (R² vs `champions_council`'s own target, KILL if > 0.98), and a shared downstream weight-to-position construction (`weights_to_target`) reusing `champions_council`'s own vol-target/deadband tail unchanged — so only the weight-vector construction differs between each candidate and the Hedge baseline. `experiments/r126_conservative_erc_council.py` (inverse-trailing-volatility ERC special case, `REBALANCE_DAYS=30`/`LOOKBACK_DAYS=90` primary, each member's std floored at 5% of the positive-std median to handle the always-zero-variance `flat` member) and `experiments/r126_novel_cvar_council.py` (Rockafellar-Uryasev CVaR-budget LP solved via dependency-free projected subgradient descent on `(w, zeta)`, Duchi et al. 2008 simplex projection, a Lagrange-multiplier bisection enforcing a trailing cross-member-median return floor, `CVAR_ALPHA=0.05`/`LOOKBACK_DAYS=90` primary) were each built by an independent agent from the frozen shared module. **Decision rule, pre-registered verbatim from the SIZE/ERR family's own convention (R-109...R-125):** PROMOTE-candidate only if the causal-truncation probe AND B1 (both markets) AND B3 (plateau majority) AND B4 (full, both markets) AND B5 all pass; B2 (drawdown) is diagnostic only. **Falsification test, pre-registered:** B4 — does the branch's `d_sharpe` sign (candidate vs `champions_council`, inner-validation) replicate on ETH? The identical test this whole research programme has used since R-59. **Configs evaluated: 31 total** (conservative 18 = 1 Step-0 + 2 B1 + 12 B3 + 1 B4 + 2 B5; novel 13 = 1 Step-0/primary fit + 2 B1 + 6 B3 + 2 B4 + 2 B5).

**Result.** Both causal-truncation probes passed (conservative: weight-schedule and target bit-identical before a 400,000-bar truncation cut, 1,386 days / 399,424 bars checked; novel: same construction, both PASS). Both Step-0 gates passed — genuinely different constructions, not rescaled copies of `champions_council`'s Hedge blend (conservative R²=−0.915, novel R²=0.573, both independently reproduced by the operator from a clean shell). Both branches' own printed max-timestamp lines read `2022-12-31 23:55:00+00:00`, never touching `OOS_START`.

**Conservative (ERC):** B1 FAILED on the conjunctive "both markets" clause — BTC spot cleared the floor decisively (`d_sharpe=+0.716`, drawdown 2.93% vs `champions_council`'s 34.49%) but futures did not (`d_sharpe=+0.092`, bootstrap CI [−0.143,+0.470] straddling zero). B3 passed with an 11/12 same-signed plateau across the `REBALANCE_DAYS`×`LOOKBACK_DAYS` grid. B4 FAILED outright: ETH spot `d_sharpe=−1.450` (bootstrap [−0.887,+0.333]), sign-inverted against BTC's +0.716 — one of the sharpest sign reversals in this project's whole BTC/ETH falsification history. B5 passed (no sign flip at 0.40%, though futures' own edge stays inside the noise floor at both tiers regardless). A disclosed mechanism: because the always-flat member's payoff is identically 0, its floored inverse-vol weight is mechanically one of the *largest* in the panel (tied with `universal_kelly` at 46.4% each by late 2022) — a meaningful share of this portfolio's apparent drawdown discipline is standing aside, not risk-budgeting among active members.

**Novel (CVaR-budgeted):** B1 PASSED both markets (`d_sharpe=+0.388` spot / `+0.537` futures, both clearing the ±0.2 floor; drawdown improved on both). Solver diagnostics: 8 of 71 fitted rebalance points needed a binding return-floor multiplier (`lam>0`), the floor was met within tolerance in 71/71, mean max-weight 0.244 (vs. a uniform 0.167) with entropy at 94% of its maximum — a well-diversified, non-degenerate solution, not a corner-collapse artifact; the pre-registered `lam`-monotonicity check held on all 8 probed windows. B3 passed with a clean 6/6 same-signed plateau (`d_sharpe` +0.24 to +0.45 across the `alpha`×`lookback` grid). B4 FAILED: ETH spot `d_sharpe=−0.530` against BTC's +0.388 — sign-inverted, the identical failure shape as the conservative branch and as five prior ERR-axis novelty-brake rounds (R-109 through R-123) and R-125's own SIZE-axis risk-measure round. B5 passed (no sign flip, moot given B4).

**Skeptic reproduction:** the operator independently re-ran `pytest tests/test_causality_strict.py` (51 passed) and independently rebuilt both branches' primary-configuration Step-0 gates from a clean shell, reusing each branch's own `build_weight_schedule` function against freshly-loaded BTC data — both R² values matched the implementing agents' own reports to the printed digit (conservative −0.915219, novel 0.573490). The conservative branch's full B1/B3/B4/B5 log was independently read end-to-end by the operator (not just the implementing agent's own summary) and every number cross-checked against the agent's final report; no discrepancy found.

**Verdict.** **NEGATIVE, both branches. Decision rule did not move** — frozen in `experiments/r126_shared.py` before either branch read a single inner-validation number, applied exactly as written; both branches stopped before touching the holdout once B1 and/or B4 failed. **The one-line lesson:** this project's Hedge/multiplicative-weights allocation across `champions_council`'s members is not obviously beatable by a risk-budgeted alternative on this data — not because risk-budgeting fails to find a real signal (the novel branch's CVaR construction is real, non-degenerate, and clears every BTC-side gate cleanly) but because whatever it is finding is a BTC-specific artifact rather than a property of risk-budgeted strategy-panel allocation: **this is the sixth distinct construction — across two different axes, and, for the first time, two different objects (`kelly_regime_v4`'s internal signal, and now `champions_council`'s cross-strategy allocation) — to pass cleanly on BTC and invert on ETH**, the strongest evidence yet that this signature belongs to the BTC/ETH training-window relationship itself rather than to any one mechanism family or even any one *object* this project's framework can vary. The conservative branch adds a second, independent lesson: an ERC/inverse-vol allocator with a naive zero-payoff floor mechanically over-weights a `flat`, always-zero-variance member — a real risk with any "inverse volatility" construction applied to a member panel that includes a standing-aside option, worth naming explicitly for any future round on this axis. **Holdout counter: +0** on top of R-125's ~698 (unchanged); running program-level total remains ~698. **This closes the `champions_council`-allocation axis as a fresh SIZE-axis line of attack** — the between-strategy portfolio object, like `kelly_regime_v4`'s own internal vote/scale, now carries a tried-and-failed risk-budgeting attempt. **Next step:** per this round's own diligence, no further axis of variation on either `kelly_regime_v4` or `champions_council` clears Step-1's non-duplicate filter without real strain; a future session should look outside both of this project's now-exhausted single-strategy and portfolio-of-strategies spaces (a genuinely new instrument class this project can fetch and simulate without proxying, or B-28's breadth clause if new low-correlation data becomes available) rather than a further variant of either construction's own internals.
